entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp

===== fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular.md
---
name: fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular
description: "fight-ai round \"ground truth\" spans are auto-seeded from the pipeline's own AI output, so scoring round IoU against them is circular"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 579b1254-323f-42d1-b482-42c5ad365f5c
---

`backend/app/services/label_span_service.py:10-34` seeds `label_spans` of kind
`round` from the `rounds` table (AI segmentation output) the first time the
Annotate page requests them, so the labeller starts pre-filled. If nobody edits
them, the "ground truth" is byte-identical to the prediction.

As of 2026-08-17 that was true of fight 46 (DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA) — 3 spans, one
shared microsecond-identical `created_at`, `labeled_at` NULL, 0 strike events,
and `segmentation_needs_review = true` with a reason calling the boundaries
"a guess". Fight 42 also matched AI output exactly; only fight 44 had a
human-adjusted round start.

**Why:** scoring round IoU against seeded spans reads 1.000 before any change
and makes every genuine segmentation *improvement* look like a regression.

**How to apply:** before trusting a round-IoU number, check whether the label
span differs from the `rounds` row and whether the span timestamps are
distinct. `eval.cli export` refuses fights with `labeled_at IS NULL`, which
catches the unfinished case but *not* the seeded-then-finished case.
Also note 3 of 4 fights were processed on the manual-labeling track and have
zero `fight_events`, so strike P/R/F1 is structurally 0 for them.
See [[easyocr-confidence-is-noise]].

===== corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground.md
---
name: corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground
description: "eval/corner_accuracy.py reads the shorts band as a fraction of bbox height, so it goes nearly blind on ground/clinch frames — a low decisive-frame count is \"unverified\", not \"fine\""
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 53047172-e54e-4eb1-a0f1-31064b2e9209
  modified: 2026-08-23T07:32:54.047Z
---

`ai/eval/corner_accuracy.py` samples each fighter's shorts band at
`_BAND_TOP=0.42` to `_BAND_BOTTOM=0.72` **of bbox height**. That geometry only
lands on the trunks when the fighter is upright. On the ground the bbox goes
wide-and-short and the band slices across arms, canvas and the opponent, so
`_colour_vote` almost never clears `_MIN_COLOUR_PX` / `_MIN_DECISIVENESS`.

Measured 2026-08-23 on DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA (a ground-heavy fight, 83 of 163 hand
labels are `ground_punch`), frames 1199–34767 at stride 15 (~2200 frames
sampled):

- fight 48 (old pipeline): **7** decisive frames
- fight 52 (new pipeline): **3** decisive frames

Whole-fight at stride 10 the same fight yields 55 decisive frames — i.e. the
evidence comes almost entirely from the standing portions elsewhere in the video.

**Why:** a whole-fight accuracy number is therefore not evenly distributed over
the fight. It can read "56% correct" while contributing essentially zero
evidence about the ground exchanges, which is exactly where tracker identity
swaps are most likely and where corner errors do the most damage to training
data.

**How to apply:** treat a low decisive-frame count as *unverified*, never as a
pass — the module's own docstring says this for the zero case and the same
applies at n=3. For ground-heavy footage, verify corners by eye
(`--verify-pose` overlay video) or via labeller-marked `corner_swap` spans
rather than trusting this number. Also note `format_accuracy` only prints runs
of >= 3 frames (`min_run`), so short flapping runs are invisible in its output —
count runs, not just accuracy, to see instability. Related:
[[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]], [[fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan]].

===== easyocr-confidence-is-noise.md
---
name: easyocr-confidence-is-noise
description: "EasyOCR line confidence on fight-ai scoreboard crops is noise-dominated (median ±0.117 from a 1px ROI change), so it cannot carry a tight threshold"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 579b1254-323f-42d1-b482-42c5ad365f5c
---

Measured 2026-08-17 on `DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA.mp4`: re-OCRing the *same* scoreboard
digits under a ≤1px change to the calibrated ROI moves EasyOCR's line
confidence by a **median of 0.117, max 0.433**. 30% of correct timer readings
straddle 0.7. So `SCOREBOARD_OCR_MIN_CONFIDENCE` gates on a quantity noisier
than any increment worth tuning, and there is a feedback loop: calibration only
unions boxes clearing the floor, so changing the floor changes the ROI, which
changes the confidences again.

**Why:** it means "tune the OCR confidence threshold" is never the right
framing for a scoreboard-coverage problem — the number is not measuring
reading quality. What actually rejects bad reads is structural: the
seconds>59/minutes>59 range check in `parsers.py` and the clock-intercept fit
in `fight_segmentation.py`.

**How to apply:** to check whether a timer read is real, don't look at
confidence — compute `k = frame/fps + seconds_remaining` and test whether it
agrees with the round's intercept. Real reads cluster within ~0.5s (the 2 Hz
sampling quantum); misreads land far off. This is a label-free correctness
check and is how the 0.7→0.5 change was validated over 4781 samples with zero
false reads. See [[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]].

===== fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan.md
---
name: fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan
description: "Agreed 3-stage plan to replace fight-ai's hand-tuned strike/state rule cascade with a trained skeleton action model"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 33d53a76-2e95-4b0d-8e5e-7581da1e9f7c
---

As of 2026-08-06, Filip and I agreed a staged plan to fix fight-ai's unreliable
punch/kick/fight-state tracking:

- **Stage 0 (in progress)** — build an eval harness before changing anything.
  Lives in `ai/eval/` (labelling tool, scorer, label-free sanity checks).
  Target ~300 labelled strikes across 2–3 fights.
- **Stage 1** — fix correctness bugs in the existing pipeline (pose→detection
  assignment collision, confidence-gate the geometry primitives, gate events to
  rounds, scale-normalise the pixel thresholds, seconds-not-frames constants).
- **Stage 2** — **chosen: train a skeleton action model** (ST-GCN / temporal CNN
  over pose sequences) to replace `detect_strikes` and `determine_fight_state`.
  Filip explicitly picked this over the alternative of a VLM-verifier-over-
  proposals approach, accepting that it is blocked on labelling first.

**Why:** the rule cascade has ~40 coupled hand-set thresholds in
`models/constants.py` and 13 commits of blind tuning with no ground truth. It
cannot be made reliable by more tuning — several constants are compensating for
bugs elsewhere rather than describing anything physical.

**How to apply:** don't propose VLM-based detection for the strike/state
problem — that fork was considered and declined. Don't change a threshold in
`constants.py` without a before/after `python -m eval.cli score` number.

===== label-events-corner-is-box-not-person.md
---
name: label-events-corner-is-box-not-person
description: "Filip labels strikes by the overlay box, not the named fighter, so label_events.corner is a track-slot pointer — the planned corner_swap flip at export would corrupt training data rather than fix it"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Stated by Filip 2026-08-31. When the overlay shows a corner swap (Roy carrying
the red box), he selects **red** and logs the punch — i.e. he picks the
rectangle around the fighter who threw it, not the fighter named red at upload.

So `label_events.corner` and `fighter_frames.corner` are **the same pointer**:
both name a track slot, not a person. Inside a `corner_swap` span they are both
"wrong" about the name and consistent about the human. The Stage 2 join
`label_events(F, corner) -> fighter_frames(F, corner) -> keypoints` therefore
already yields correct training rows with nothing applied.

**Why:** it inverts the design in the plan. Applying the swap at export — as
`ai/eval/schema.py:152` ("Applied at export time when joining labels to
fighter_frames.keypoints") and `plan/02c-labelling-ui.md:156` ("flips red/blue
in the exported training tensor") both instruct — would attach the label to the
*other* fighter's skeleton. That is the exact silent corruption
`plan/02a-upload-tracks.md:95` set out to prevent, caused by the mitigation.
The premise there was identity-labelling; the actual convention is
box-labelling, under which the corruption never existed.

**How to apply:** never apply `corner_swaps` to a label-to-keypoint join. Apply
it only where a *person* is needed (per-fighter stats, `fight_events.fighter_id`),
and at read time — mutating `fighter_frames.corner` would desync it from
`label_events.corner` and break the join that currently works. Two knock-ons:
`score.py:225`'s "fighter attribution %" is circular (the labeller read the
corner off the pipeline's own overlay, so it can never detect a swap — cf.
[[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]]); and span *boundary* error no longer
corrupts training data as `plan/02d-label-quality.md:213` claims, though
detection rate still matters for the tracker metric. The spans remain the
ground truth for [[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]], which is now their
main purpose. See also [[corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground]].

===== frontend-palette-collisions.md
---
name: frontend-palette-collisions
description: "Annotate timeline's CLINCH orange and GROUND red are indistinguishable (normal-vision ΔE 6.6), GROUND reuses the red-corner colour, and status red ≈ corner red; a validated state trio exists"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c7387d42-ce46-4661-b2cf-4a0399517e3e
  modified: 2026-09-10T07:50:45.751Z
---

Measured 2026-09-10 with the dataviz skill's `validate_palette.js`, dark mode,
surface `#0f1113` (a glass card over the `#050709` page):

- `AnnotationTimeline.tsx` STATE lane: STRIKING `#00daf3`, CLINCH `#ff7043`,
  GROUND `#ff4d4d`. CLINCH↔GROUND normal-vision ΔE **6.6** (floor 15), deutan
  ΔE 4.2 — hard to tell apart even with full colour vision. GROUND is also
  `--f-red`, the red corner.
- Status red `--red-500 #ef4444` vs `--f-red #ff4d4d`: ΔE 3.7 — a fail badge next
  to red-corner marks reads as the same colour.
- good `#0ca30c` vs critical `#ef4444`: deutan ΔE 3.1 — status needs icon + text.
- Passes every check, all pairs: STRIKING `#0099b0` (`--cyan-600`), CLINCH
  `#e64a19` (`--orange-600`), GROUND `#9085e9` (no token yet). The red/blue corner
  pair is fine (CVD ΔE 25.9).
- Contrast on `#0f1113`: `--text-disabled #475569` 2.5:1, `--text-muted #64748b`
  4.0:1 — neither is safe for data labels.

**Why:** the design-system accents are neon-bright and were chosen by eye; these
collisions only show up when measured.

**How to apply:** use the validated trio for any state-coloured chart (it is what
`frontend/TRAINING_LAB_BRIEF.md` §14 specifies for the planned `/lab` page), and
run the validator before adding a categorical colour instead of picking from
`frontend/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` by eye.

content.content:
1	# Training Lab — design brief
2	
3	> **For Claude Design.** Paste this whole file. It describes a new page for the
4	> Fight.AI web app: a dashboard over hand-labelled training data and the
5	> pipeline's measured accuracy. Every number under "Sample" is **illustrative** —
6	> realistic in shape, modelled on the fights in this repo, not a live snapshot.
7	> The visual language must match the existing app (§14).
8	
9	## 1. Context
10	
11	Fight.AI turns MMA fight video into structured events. A Python pipeline detects
12	both fighters, tracks them, estimates 17-point pose skeletons, assigns red/blue
13	corners, reads the scoreboard to find rounds, then runs a hand-tuned rule cascade
14	that emits strikes (`jab_head`, `ground_punch`, …) and fight state
15	(STRIKING / CLINCH / GROUND).
16	
17	That rule cascade is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model, which is
18	blocked on **labelled data**. A human watches a fight in the **Annotate** page and
19	logs every strike, state change, takedown, round boundary, corner swap and
20	excluded stretch. The target is **~300 labelled strikes across 2–3 fights**
21	(~10–15 min of round time) before training; ~50 is already useful for evaluation.
22	
23	A labelled fight becomes one of two things, never both:
24	
25	- **Training fight** — its labels and skeletons feed the model.
26	- **Evaluation fixture** — it is re-run through the full AI pipeline and the
27	  predictions are scored against the labels (strike precision/recall/F1, fight
28	  state, rounds).
29	
30	Today all of this lives in CLI output (`python -m eval.cli summary | score |
31	sanity`). The Training Lab puts it on one page.
32	
33	## 2. Users and the questions the page answers
34	
35	Users: 1–3 pipeline developers who label fights and change the pipeline.
36	Technical, data-literate, rightly suspicious of any unqualified number.
37	Desktop-first.
38	
39	In priority order, the page must answer:
40	
41	1. **How much labelled data do we have, of which kinds, and how far are we from
42	   the 300-strike target?**
43	2. **Is it trainable?** Which classes are starved? Is one fight dominating?
44	3. **What is the pipeline's current accuracy — and how far can that number be
45	   trusted?**
46	4. **Did the last pipeline change help or hurt?** Against the frozen baseline and
47	   the previous version.
48	5. **Is the ground truth itself healthy?** Rounds confirmed, swaps marked, no open
49	   spans, source video still on disk, exported to git.
50	6. **What should I do next?** Finish labelling X, export Y, re-run Z as a fixture,
51	   fix a failing check.
52	
53	**10-second test:** someone opening the page cold can say "213 of 300 strikes,
54	ground punches dominate, strike F1 isn't measurable yet because no labelled fight
55	has predictions."
56	
57	## 3. Honesty rules — design these in, they are the point of the page
58	
59	This project has been misled repeatedly by numbers that looked fine. Each rule
60	matches a real trap in this codebase.
61	
62	1. **Every metric shows its n and its provenance.** F1 always travels with the
63	   ground-truth strike count, the fixture count, the matching tolerance
64	   (±0.25 s = ±12 frames at 50 fps) and the pipeline version (short git SHA +
65	   constants hash). No bare percentages.
66	2. **"Not measured", "Not scorable" and "Unverified" are first-class states —
67	   never 0%, never blank.** A labelled fight processed on the manual track has no
68	   predictions: its F1 is *not scorable*, not 0%.
69	3. **Circular metrics are visibly flagged, or hidden.**
70	   - *Corner read-back* (the labeller's corner matches the pipeline's on matched
71	     strikes) reads ~100% by construction: the labeller clicks the overlay box the
72	     pipeline drew, so a tracker swap is copied into the label. Never call it
73	     "attribution accuracy". It sits behind a `Circular` badge.
74	   - *Round IoU* is circular when the labelled round spans were auto-seeded from
75	     the pipeline's own output and never edited. Show `Seeded — not verified`
76	     instead of an IoU.
77	4. **Lower bounds say so.** Corner-swap coverage (share of round time inside
78	   labeller-marked swap spans) is a *lower bound* on corner-assignment error until
79	   labeller swap recall is measured. Render it as `≥ 4.4%`.
80	5. **Low evidence is not a pass.** A label-free corner check with few decisive
81	   frames is `Unverified`, even when it reads 100%.
82	6. **Accuracy is shown against the human ceiling.** With a double-labelling
83	   agreement measurement: `F1 56.7% · human ceiling 91.4%`. Without one:
84	   `ceiling not measured`. An F1 with no ceiling can't be judged good or bad.
85	7. **Fight state leads with stability, not per-frame accuracy.** Per-frame
86	   accuracy is dominated by the most common state and stays high while the state
87	   machine visibly flaps. Lead with transitions/min and median dwell, truth vs
88	   predicted.
89	8. **Numbers are only comparable at the same tolerance and on the same fixture
90	   set.** A trend line breaks (gap plus a note) wherever either changes.
91	
92	## 4. Placement and layout
93	
94	- **Nav:** add **Lab** to the header after Analysis and Library (the app already
95	  uses "Lab Report" wording). Route `/lab`. Page title "Training Lab", subtitle
96	  "Labelled data and pipeline accuracy".
97	- **Width:** max 1440 px, centred, 22 px / 30 px page padding — same as the Player.
98	- **One scrolling page**, with a compact sticky section index on wide screens:
99	  1. Filter row
100	  2. **A** Overview
101	  3. **B** Annotated events
102	  4. **C** Spans & coverage
103	  5. **D** Fight ledger
104	  6. **E** Pipeline accuracy
105	  7. **F** Pipeline health (label-free)
106	  8. **G** Label quality & action queue
107	  - A reference drawer (taxonomy mapping, §13) opens from section B's header.
108	- **Grid:** 12 columns, 14 px gaps. Every section is a glass card (§14).
109	
110	## 5. Filter row
111	
112	One left-aligned row under the page title. It scopes everything below it.
113	
114	- **Fights:** pills `All labelled` · `Training` · `Evaluation fixtures` ·
115	  `In progress`, plus a multi-select fight combobox.
116	- **Labelling period:** `All time` · `Last 7 days` · `Last 30 days`. Affects the
117	  activity chart and the "added" deltas only.
118	- **Pipeline version** (scopes E and F): dropdown of scored versions, newest first,
119	  rows like `807c1b6 · constants a41f… · 10 Sep`; `Working tree (uncommitted)`
120	  flagged with a dot.
121	- Far right: `Refreshed 2 min ago` and a refresh icon button. A refetch keeps the
122	  previous render at reduced opacity — no skeleton flash, no layout jump.
123	
124	## 6. A · Overview
125	
126	One **hero card** and a row of stat tiles. The hero is training-set progress — the
127	user's first question. Accuracy is the most prominent tile, with detail in E.
128	
129	**Hero card — Training set progress** (~5 columns)
130	
131	- Hero figure **213 / 300 strikes**, in the app's stat face.
132	- A meter beneath it: fill = strikes labelled, track = a lighter step of the same
133	  hue. Ticks at **50** ("useful for evaluation") and **300** ("training target").
134	- `71% · 87 to go · ~26 days at the last-14-day pace (3.4 strikes/day)`
135	- `18.4 min of labelled round time across 3 fights`
136	
137	**Stat tiles**
138	
139	| Tile | Sample value | Sub-line |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| Label events | 250 | +59 in the last 14 days · includes state marks |
142	| Fights | 3 labelled | 2 finished · 1 in progress · 1 exported to git |
143	| Largest-fight share | 67% | DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA — warning above 50%: the model would mostly learn one bout |
144	| Strike detection F1 | `Not scorable` | "No evaluation fixture yet" · populated: `56.7%` · P 62.9 · R 51.7 · n = 118 · ceiling not measured |
145	| Sanity checks | 7 / 9 | latest AI run · JURIC vs NOGUEIRA |
146	
147	Clicking a tile scrolls to its section.
148	
149	## 7. B · Annotated events — "what have we labelled?"
150	
151	The core section. Card header: title, total (`213 strikes · 37 other events`), a
152	view toggle, a `Table` toggle, and the reference-drawer icon.
153	
154	### B1. Events by type
155	
156	**Form:** a horizontal bar list, one row per palette action, grouped under the
157	Annotate palette's own group names. All bars share one hue (cyan): the row label
158	carries identity, so no per-row colours. Each row:
159	
160	`[key] Label ········ [bar] count · share · R|B split · trains-as · scored status`
161	
162	- **Key chip** — the Annotate shortcut (`1`, `c`, `v` …) in a small inner tile, so
163	  labellers can map the row to the palette. Group note for hand strikes:
164	  "⇧ = body".
165	- **R|B split** — a thin two-segment bar under the main bar (red / blue, 2 px
166	  surface gap) or `R 19 · B 14`. Tooltip: "Corner = the overlay box the labeller
167	  clicked (a track slot), not a named fighter."
168	- **Trains-as chip** — the export family: `hook`, `kick · leg`,
169	  `punch · non-specific`.
170	- **Scored status** (icon + label):
171	  - `Scored` — has a pipeline counterpart
172	  - `Always a miss` — elbow: the pipeline has no elbow detector, so every labelled
173	    elbow is a false negative
174	  - `Captured only` — exported, not yet scored (takedown landed)
175	  - `Not exported` — takedown attempt/defended, submission, knockdown, fight end
176	- **Minimum-examples marker** — a hairline at the per-class minimum (default 25,
177	  editable from the card menu). Rows under it get a small `Low` warning chip.
178	
179	**View toggle:** `Palette actions` (default) · `Training classes` (collapsed to
180	export families: jab, cross, hook, uppercut, elbow, knee, kick, punch) ·
181	`By fight` (small multiples, one mini list per fight, shared x-scale).
182	
183	**Sample — palette actions, all labelled fights**
184	
185	| Group | Action | Key | Count | R | B | Trains as | Status |
186	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
187	| Strikes | Jab | 1 | 33 | 19 | 14 | jab | Scored |
188	| | Cross | 2 | 20 | 11 | 9 | cross | Scored |
189	| | Left hook | 3 | 9 | 5 | 4 | hook | Scored |
190	| | Right hook | 4 | 14 | 8 | 6 | hook | Scored |
191	| | Left uppercut | 5 | 2 | 1 | 1 | uppercut | Scored |
192	| | Right uppercut | 6 | 3 | 2 | 1 | uppercut | Scored |
193	| | Calf kick | c | 8 | 3 | 5 | kick · leg | Scored |
194	| | Low kick | l | 7 | 4 | 3 | kick · leg | Scored |
195	| | Middle kick | m | 5 | 2 | 3 | kick · body | Scored |
196	| | High kick | h | 3 | 1 | 2 | kick · head | Scored |
197	| | Elbow | e | 3 | 3 | 0 | elbow | Always a miss |
198	| | Clinch knee | n | 5 | 2 | 3 | knee · non-specific | Scored |
199	| Ground & pound | Clinch punch | u | 10 | 6 | 4 | punch · non-specific | Scored |
200	| | Ground and pound | v | 87 | 49 | 38 | punch · non-specific | Scored |
201	| | Ground knee | j | 4 | 2 | 2 | knee · non-specific | Scored |
202	| Grappling | Takedown attempt | t | 5 | 3 | 2 | — | Not exported |
203	| | Takedown landed | y | 4 | 3 | 1 | takedown | Captured only |
204	| | Takedown defended | d | 2 | 1 | 1 | — | Not exported |
205	| | Submission | s | 1 | 1 | 0 | — | Not exported |
206	| Outcome | Knockdown | x | 1 | 1 | 0 | — | Not exported |
207	| Fight state | Striking | w | 10 | — | — | state span | Scored |
208	| | Clinch | f | 6 | — | — | state span | Scored |
209	| | Ground | g | 6 | — | — | state span | Scored |
210	| Other | Fight end | modal | 2 | — | — | — | Not exported |
211	
212	### B2. Training classes — family × target
213	
214	**Form:** a heatmap. Rows = families, columns = head · body · leg · non-specific,
215	each cell showing its count. One sequential hue (cyan ramp), count text in white
216	or ink chosen by the cell's luminance. Cells under the minimum get a small warning
217	tick in the corner. `—` cells are impossible combinations (drawn empty, not zero).
218	
219	| Family | head | body | leg | non-specific | Total |
220	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
221	| jab | 26 | 7 | — | — | 33 |
222	| cross | 16 | 4 | — | — | 20 |
223	| hook | 18 | 5 | — | — | 23 |
224	| uppercut | 4 | 1 | — | — | 5 |
225	| elbow | 2 | 1 | — | — | 3 |
226	| kick | 3 | 5 | 15 | — | 23 |
227	| knee | — | — | — | 9 | 9 |
228	| punch | — | — | — | 97 | 97 |
229	| **Total** | **69** | **23** | **15** | **106** | **213** |
230	
231	Caption: "107 specific · 106 non-specific. At ~300 strikes the first model will
232	collapse target (and probably family) — the labels keep the distinction for
233	later."
234	
235	### B3. Strikes by fight state
236	
237	**Form:** a 100% stacked horizontal bar per training family plus one overall bar.
238	Segments: STRIKING · CLINCH · GROUND · before first state mark, in the state
239	colours from §14. Legend always shown; direct labels only on segments wide enough
240	to hold them.
241	
242	Sample overall: STRIKING 92 · CLINCH 21 · GROUND 98 · no state yet 2.
243	
244	Callout: "46% of strikes happened on the ground; 83 of the 87 ground-and-pound
245	punches come from one fight."
246	
247	### B4. Labelling activity
248	
249	**Form:** a column chart of label events per day (last 30 days), one hue. The
250	tooltip breaks a day down by fight. Cumulative strikes against the 300 target go
251	in a separate small line chart underneath, sharing the x-axis — never a second
252	y-axis on the same plot.
253	
254	Sample: 15 Aug 16 · 19 Aug 38 · 20 Aug 52 · 21 Aug 41 · 22 Aug 32 · 26 Aug 12 ·
255	29 Aug 18 · 2 Sep 9 · 5 Sep 22 · 9 Sep 10.
256	
257	## 8. C · Spans & coverage — "is the ground truth complete?"
258	
259	Three compact cards in a row, then a coverage strip per fight.
260	
261	**C1. Rounds confirmed** — per fight: `3 rounds · 2 adjusted · 1 seeded`. Each
262	round carries a status: `Adjusted by hand` (good) or `Seeded, unchanged`
263	(warning; tooltip: "identical to the pipeline's own segmentation — round accuracy
264	measured against it is circular").
265	Sample: DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA 2 adjusted / 1 seeded · VITASOVIC vs STOSIC 0 / 3
266	seeded (in progress) · MILIDRAGOVIC vs MOOSMAN 1 adjusted.
267	
268	**C2. Corner swaps** — count, total duration, share of labelled round time,
269	always rendered as a lower bound.
270	Sample: DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA `5 · 25 s · ≥ 4.4%` · VITASOVIC vs STOSIC
271	`8 · 2.4 min · ≥ 16%` · MILIDRAGOVIC vs MOOSMAN `0 marked` (never "0% error").
272	Footnote: "Lower bound — labeller swap recall not measured yet (see G1)."
273	
274	**C3. Excluded** — count, total duration, reason chips.
275	Sample: DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA 2 (replay 14 s, camera cut 3 s) · VITASOVIC vs
276	STOSIC 1 (replay 9 s) · MILIDRAGOVIC vs MOOSMAN 1 (no reason given).
277	
278	**C4. Coverage strip** (one per fight, full width) — the whole video as a thin
279	timeline, borrowing the Annotate timeline's lanes at miniature scale:
280	
281	- **Rounds** — green blocks; a seeded-unchanged round gets a dashed outline.
282	- **State** — segments in the state colours.
283	- **Swaps / excluded** — purple / muted blocks, as in Annotate.
284	- **Label density** — a one-row heat strip of strikes per 10 s (cyan ramp). A
285	  stretch *inside a round* with no labels lights up as `Unlabelled stretch`. This
286	  is the strip's main job: it shows "round 2 only labelled up to 3:10".
287	- Hover shows time, frame and counts. Clicking opens Annotate at that frame. That
288	  needs a new `?frame=` URL parameter — neither Annotate nor the Player accepts
289	  one today.
290	
291	## 9. D · Fight ledger
292	
293	A dense table, one row per fight (labelled or AI-processed). Sticky header,
294	sortable columns, click a row to expand.
295	
296	| Column | Content |
297	|---|---|
298	| Fight | `DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA`, grey sub-line `#52 · 50 fps · 11.9 min` |
299	| Track | `Manual` or `AI` pill |
300	| Lifecycle | Five linked dots: Processed → Labelling → Finished → Exported → Scored. Filled = done, ring = current, faint = not yet. "Exported" = `ai/eval/labels/<video>.json` exists; add `Stale` when the database changed after export |
301	| Role | `Training` · `Eval fixture` · `Unlabelled` · `⚠ Both` (critical: the same bout is used for training and for evaluation — including a re-upload of the same video under another id) |
302	| Round min | Labelled round time |
303	| Strikes | Count, plus density per minute (warning under 5/min on a finished fight — probably unfinished) |
304	| State marks | Count |
305	| Swaps | `5 · ≥ 4.4%` |
306	| Excluded | Count |
307	| Sanity | `7/9` with tiny pass/fail pips (AI runs only) |
308	| Corner check | `95% · 219 fr` · `Unverified · 17 fr` · `Not run` |
309	| Strike F1 | Fixtures only; `Not scorable` on manual-track fights |
310	| Warnings | Count badge; opens the row's list |
311	| Actions | Icon buttons: Open in Annotate, Open in Player, copy-command menu (`export`, `sanity`, `score`, `corner_accuracy`) |
312	
313	**Expanded row:** the coverage strip (C4) full width, a mini event-mix bar list
314	(top 6 actions), the warnings list, last labelled date, labeller name(s), and the
315	segmentation verdict — source `Clock` or `Detection only`, with the pipeline's
316	review reason verbatim.
317	
318	**Sample rows**
319	
320	| Fight | Track | Lifecycle | Role | Round min | Strikes · /min | Swaps | Sanity | Corner check | F1 | Warn |
321	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
322	| DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA | Manual | Finished 22 Aug, not exported | Training | 9.4 | 143 · 15.2 | 5 · ≥ 4.4% | — | 58% · 55 fr · swaps | Not scorable | 4 |
323	| VITASOVIC vs STOSIC | Manual | Labelling | Training | 6.1 of 15 | 58 · 9.5 | 8 · ≥ 16% | — | Not run | Not scorable | 3 |
324	| MILIDRAGOVIC vs MOOSMAN | Manual | Exported 15 Aug | Training | 2.9 | 12 · 4.1 ⚠ | 0 | — | 93% · 86 fr | Not scorable | 3 |
325	| NAZHAND vs STAROPOLI | AI | Processed | Unlabelled | — | — | — | 8/9 | 95% · 219 fr | — | 1 |
326	| JURIC vs NOGUEIRA | AI | Processed | Unlabelled | — | — | — | 7/9 | Unverified · 17 fr | — | 1 |
327	
328	**Sample warnings**
329	
330	- DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA — not exported to git · round 3 span seeded, never adjusted ·
331	  segmentation needs review ("round count came from fighter detection alone") ·
332	  bout uploaded 3 times (#46, #48, #52), 2 of those source videos missing on disk.
333	  Its corner check draws its decisive frames almost entirely from standing
334	  exchanges, so the ground sequences are unverified. Show that as gaps in the
335	  expanded row's evidence strip.
336	- VITASOVIC vs STOSIC — 1 corner-swap span still open (export will skip it) ·
337	  corner assignment fell back to the legacy path ("ambiguous tape: both slots read
338	  blue") · rounds 2–3 not reviewed yet.
339	- MILIDRAGOVIC vs MOOSMAN — low label density (4.1 strikes/min) on a finished
340	  fight · no labeller recorded · excluded span has no reason.
341	- NAZHAND vs STAROPOLI — not labelled; candidate evaluation fixture.
342	- JURIC vs NOGUEIRA — sanity: strike rate implausible (3.1/min, expected 5–60).
343	
344	## 10. E · Pipeline accuracy — "how good is it, and can I trust the number?"
345	
346	A provenance line sits under the section title, always visible:
347	`Pipeline 807c1b6 · constants a41f… · tolerance ±0.25 s (±12 f at 50 fps) ·
348	2 fixtures · 118 labelled strikes`
349	
350	### E0. Not measurable yet — today's real state, design it first
351	
352	Every fight labelled so far was processed on the manual track, so there are no
353	predictions to score. The section must say so plainly instead of showing zeros:
354	
355	> **Strike accuracy isn't measurable yet.** The labelled fights have no pipeline
356	> predictions. Re-run a finished fight through the AI pipeline to make it an
357	> evaluation fixture — and keep it out of the training set.
358	> `python main.py fight_videos/<video>` then
359	> `python -m eval.cli score fight_videos/<video> --json <path>`
360	> [Choose a fixture ▾] [Copy commands]
361	
362	Below the message, point to what does work without fixtures: pipeline health (F)
363	and label quality (G).
364	
365	### E1. Headline — populated state (illustrative)
366	
367	A group of stat tiles, not a wall of gauges:
368	
369	- **Strike detection F1 56.7%** (large), `P 62.9% · R 51.7%`,
370	  `TP 61 · FP 36 · FN 57`, `118 labelled · 97 predicted`.
371	- **Human ceiling** `Not measured`, linking to G1. Once measured: a 0–100% track
372	  with the F1 fill and a tick at the ceiling (e.g. 91.4%).
373	- **Change** `+7.2 pts vs 53ee95d · +25.5 pts vs baseline/pre-stage-1`. Neutral
374	  grey with "not comparable" when tolerance or fixture set differ.
375	- Footnote: "Pooled over fixtures — TP/FP/FN summed, then P/R/F1 computed. Not an
376	  average of per-fight F1."

379	
380	| Fixture | Labelled | Predicted | TP / FP / FN | P | R | F1 | Bias · jitter | Scored at |
381	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
382	| NAZHAND vs STAROPOLI | 74 | 61 | 40 / 21 / 34 | 65.6% | 54.1% | 59.3% | +3 f · 4 f | 807c1b6 |
383	| JURIC vs NOGUEIRA | 44 | 36 | 21 / 15 / 23 | 58.3% | 47.7% | 52.5% | +3 f · 5 f | 807c1b6 |

388	### E3. Classification — matched strikes only
389	
390	Four stat tiles, each with its own n:
391	
392	- **Strike family 41.0%** · 39 specific matches
393	- **Target zone 71.8%** · 39
394	- **Landed vs missed** `Not measurable` — labels deliberately record no outcome
395	- **Grappling matches 22** — non-specific predictions (clinch/ground punches and
396	  knees): counted for detection, excluded from family and target
397	
398	A collapsed row underneath: **Corner read-back 98.4% · 61**, with a `Circular`
399	badge and the explanation: "The labeller picks the corner from the pipeline's own
400	overlay, so a tracker swap is copied into the label and cancels out. Use corner
401	swaps (C2) and the label-free corner check (F2) instead."
402	
403	### E4. Family confusion
404	
405	**Form:** a heatmap, truth rows × predicted columns (jab, cross, hook, uppercut,
406	elbow, kick), row-normalised %, one sequential hue, the diagonal value in bold
407	text. Beside it, the top confusions as a short list:
408	`hook → uppercut 4 · jab → cross 4 · cross → jab 3 · cross → hook 3`.
409	Note on the elbow row: "No pipeline equivalent — every labelled elbow is a miss."
410	
411	### E5. Timing
412	
413	A dot strip of signed offsets (predicted − labelled, in frames) from −12 to +12,
414	with a zero line. Stats: `bias +3.0 f (60 ms late) · jitter 4.5 f`.
415	Caption: "Bias is a constant to subtract once, not a reason to widen the
416	tolerance."
417	
418	### E6. Fight state
419	
420	- **Dumbbell rows** (truth dot — predicted dot on one shared axis per row):
421	  - Transitions per minute: truth 2.1 · predicted 6.8, with a warning badge
422	    "flaps 3× faster than reality"
423	  - Median dwell: truth 14.2 s · predicted 3.1 s
424	- A 3×3 confusion heatmap, STRIKING / CLINCH / GROUND, row-normalised.
425	- Per-frame accuracy 78.2%, deliberately small, captioned "dominated by the most
426	  common state".
427	
428	### E7. Rounds
429	
430	Per fixture: `Count ✓ 3 = 3`, then per round IoU with start/end offsets.
431	Sample: R1 IoU 97.9% (start +0.8 s, end −0.4 s) · R2 96.4% (+1.9 s, −2.4 s) ·
432	R3 `Seeded — not verified`.
433	Note: "Splitting one round into three still gives a high IoU — the count is what
434	catches it."
435	
436	### E8. Trend across pipeline versions
437	
438	**Form:** a line chart. x = pipeline versions in commit order (short SHA + date),
439	y = 0–100%, one y-axis.
440	
441	- F1 in the accent colour: 2 px line, ≥ 8 px markers.
442	- Precision and recall in de-emphasis grey, direct-labelled at the line ends.
443	- Human ceiling as a labelled horizontal reference line, once measured.
444	- The baseline version carries a flag; a different marker glyph wherever
445	  `constants.py` changed.
446	- The line breaks with a note wherever tolerance or the fixture set changed.
447	
448	Sample F1: baseline/pre-stage-1 31.2 · 5ecd0ba 44.0 · 53ee95d 49.5 · 807c1b6 56.7.
449	
450	### E9. Worst misses and false positives
451	
452	Two short lists side by side, 8 rows each, missed strikes first — they are the
453	review queue. Row: clock, frame, corner dot, what was labelled or predicted,
454	fixture. Clicking a row opens Annotate or the Player at that frame.
455	
456	- `2:14.36 · f6719 · R · labelled left hook · head · not detected`
457	- `3:02.10 · f9106 · B · predicted jab_head · no label within ±12 f`
458	
459	## 11. F · Pipeline health — label-free, works on every processed fight
460	
461	These checks need no labels. They catch output that is *internally impossible*,
462	not merely inaccurate, so they run on every AI-processed fight. The corner and
463	segmentation parts also apply to manual-track fights, which run every stage
464	except strike detection and the state machine.
465	
466	### F1. Sanity checks
467	
468	**Form:** a matrix. Rows = processed fights, columns = the 9 checks, cells = a
469	status icon: `Pass` · `Fail` · `Not evaluated` (e.g. "no state transitions to
470	evaluate"). Hover shows the measured value, the detail and the expected band. A
471	summary column reads `7 / 9`. A `Compare with previous version` toggle adds a
472	small arrow badge to every cell that changed — flipped to pass (good) or to fail
473	(critical).
474	
475	| Check | Expected band |
476	|---|---|
477	| Events inside rounds | 0% of strikes outside a round |
478	| No simultaneous mutual strikes | ≤ 2% of events |
479	| No duplicate events | 0 |
480	| State does not flap | ≤ 15 transitions/min |
481	| State dwell is physical | median ≥ 1.0 s |
482	| Strike rate is plausible | 5–60 strikes/min |
483	| No short interior rounds | 0 |
484	| Round breaks are real breaks | 0 gaps too short |
485	| Round count fits video length | ≤ what the video can hold |
486	
487	Sample history (these are the real committed baseline reports for JURIC vs
488	NOGUEIRA):
489	
490	- `769e83f` — 2 of 6 pass: mutual strikes 75% ✕, duplicate events 4 ✕,
491	  19.6 transitions/min ✕, dwell 0.76 s ✕. The 3 round checks didn't exist yet —
492	  `Not evaluated`.
493	- `5ecd0ba` — 3 of 4 pass: strike rate 3.1/min ✕. State checks `Not evaluated`
494	  (no transitions); round checks `Not evaluated`.
495	
496	### F2. Corner assignment (per fight)
497	
498	- **Label-free corner check** — `95% correct · 219 decisive frames` → `OK`.
499	  Below 90% → `Intermittent swaps` (warning). Below 50% → `Inverted` (critical).
500	  Fewer decisive frames than a minimum (proposed default 30) → `Unverified`,
501	  whatever the percentage. A thin strip along the fight's timeline shows OK and
502	  flipped runs, plus the gaps where no frame was decisive (typically ground
503	  sequences).
504	- **Assignment path** — `Appearance` · `Legacy fallback — ambiguous tape (both
505	  slots read blue)` · `Legacy fallback — too few clean frames`.
506	- **Clean frames per slot** — `412 / 388`.
507	- **Duplicate-corner invariant** — `OK` or `Violated` (critical: a release
508	  blocker).
509	- **Box/skeleton drift** — `0.62% of rows` (the skeleton's torso centre falls
510	  outside its own box).
511	
512	Sample: JURIC vs NOGUEIRA `100% · 17 fr → Unverified` · MILIDRAGOVIC vs MOOSMAN
513	`93% · 86 fr → OK` · NAZHAND vs STAROPOLI `95% · 219 fr → OK` · DRAGOJEVIC vs
514	HONDA `58% · 55 fr → Intermittent swaps`.
515	
516	### F3. Segmentation and source video
517	
518	- **Round source** — `Clock` (scoreboard timer fitted) or `Detection only`
519	  (warning: "boundaries are a guess"), timer coverage %, round-number coverage %,
520	  and the pipeline's review reason verbatim.
521	- **Video integrity** — `reported 35,589 · decoded 35,589 frames ✓` and
522	  `File on disk ✓ / ✕`. Tooltip: "Labels point at frames of this exact file. A
523	  missing or re-encoded video detaches every label."
524	
525	## 12. G · Label quality & action queue
526	
527	### G1. Can we trust the labels?
528	
529	Three status cards:
530	
531	- **Human agreement ceiling** — `Not measured`. "Label one round twice — a second
532	  person, or yourself a week later — to get a ceiling for every F1." Once
533	  measured: detection F1, family agreement, corner agreement (expect ~100%; lower
534	  means a labelling-UI defect) and the most common disagreements.
535	- **Corner-swap recall** — `Not run`. "Inject a known swap, label the fight
536	  normally, check the swap got marked." Once run: detected or missed, plus start
537	  and end edge error in frames.
538	- **Matching tolerance** — `±0.25 s, pinned`. A range bar from a floor (p95 of
539	  human timing jitter — needs the agreement run) to a ceiling (p5 of the gap
540	  between one fighter's consecutive strikes — computable from labels today), with
541	  the current value marked. Critical when the current value is above the ceiling:
542	  "fast combinations can shift-match and inflate F1". Sample ceiling: 0.18 s →
543	  critical.
544	
545	### G2. Action queue
546	
547	A prioritised list grouped by severity. Each item: status icon + label, fight,
548	a one-line explanation, one action (`Open at frame` · `Copy command` ·
549	`Snooze 7 days`).
550	
551	- **Critical:** same bout used for training and evaluation · duplicate-corner
552	  invariant violated · tolerance above the combination ceiling · source video
553	  missing for a labelled fight
554	- **Warning:** open span (export skips it) · strikes outside every round span
555	  (dropped on export) · state mark with a corner attached · labels after the
556	  fight-end mark · finished but not exported · export older than the latest
557	  labels · round span seeded and never adjusted · segmentation needs review · low
558	  label density on a finished fight · one fight above 50% of strikes · class below
559	  the minimum · corner check unverified or intermittent · failing sanity check
560	- **Info:** events captured but not exported (takedown attempt/defended,
561	  submission, knockdown, fight end) · no labeller name · human ceiling not
562	  measured · swap recall not run
563	
564	Sample top of queue:
565	
566	1. Critical · all fights — tolerance ±0.25 s is above the combination ceiling
567	   (0.18 s) · `Copy command`
568	2. Critical · #48 DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA (earlier upload) — source video missing; its
569	   labels can't be joined back to frames · `Open fight`
570	3. Warning · VITASOVIC vs STOSIC — corner-swap span open since 4:12 ·
571	   `Open at frame`
572	4. Warning · DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA — finished 22 Aug, not exported ·
573	   `Copy command`
574	5. Warning · all fights — one fight holds 67% of strikes; label more of the
575	   others · `Open ledger`
576	
577	## 13. Reference drawer — how labels become training data and scores
578	
579	A right-side drawer, opened from section B's header.
580	
581	| Palette action | Exports as (family · target) | Scored against | Note |
582	|---|---|---|---|
583	| Jab · Cross | jab / cross · head or body | `jab_head` … `cross_body` | lead/rear hand — works for southpaws |
584	| Left/right hook · left/right uppercut | hook / uppercut · head or body | `hook_*` · `uppercut_*` | the hand is dropped at export |
585	| Calf kick · Low kick | kick · leg | `low_kick` | |
586	| Middle kick | kick · body | `middle_kick` | |
587	| High kick | kick · head | `head_kick` | |
588	| Elbow | elbow · head or body | — | always a miss until the pipeline detects elbows |
589	| Clinch knee · Ground knee | knee · non-specific | `clinch_knee` · `ground_knee` | counts for detection only |
590	| Clinch punch · Ground and pound | punch · non-specific | `clinch_punch` · `ground_punch` | counts for detection only |
591	| Striking · Clinch · Ground marks | state spans, each running to the next mark or the end of its round | state changes | |
592	| Takedown landed | takedown | `takedown_initiated` | captured, not yet scored |
593	| Takedown attempt/defended · Submission · Knockdown · Fight end | not exported | — | |
594	
595	Drawer footer: "Matching is optimal one-to-one on time within ±0.25 s, ignoring
596	corner. Only frames inside a labelled round and outside every excluded span
597	count."
598	
599	## 14. Visual system
600	
601	Match the existing app (`frontend/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`):
602	
603	- **Background** `#050709` with the drifting cyan / purple / orange ambient orbs
604	  and ~3% film grain.
605	- **Glass cards:** fill `rgba(255,255,255,0.04)`, `blur(20px) saturate(160%)`,
606	  1 px `rgba(255,255,255,0.07)` border, 16 px radius, 18 / 20 px padding.
607	  **Inner tiles:** `rgba(0,0,0,0.30)`, 1 px `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` border,
608	  12 px radius.
609	- **Type:** Manrope for UI (400–800); Bebas Neue for large stat numbers only;
610	  section labels 10.5 px, 700, uppercase, 0.12 em tracking; headings 800 with the
611	  white-to-50% gradient fill.
612	- **Icons:** Material Symbols Outlined, 14–22 px.
613	- **Controls:** pills for toggles, glass buttons for secondary actions, the cyan
614	  gradient primary button for at most one action per view.
615	- **Motion:** sections fade up on first load (0.5 s, staggered 80 ms). Nothing
616	  animates on refetch.
617	
618	**Colour roles** — checked with a palette validator against the card surface
619	(≈ `#0f1113`), including simulated colour blindness:
620	
621	| Role | Colours | Rule |
622	|---|---|---|
623	| Magnitude — bars, heatmaps, meters | cyan ramp from `#00daf3` | one hue; nominal categories never get a colour each |
624	| Corner | red `#ff4d4d` · blue `#3aa0ff` | clearly separable for all readers; always paired with an R/B label or the fighter's name |
625	| Fight state (charts on this page) | STRIKING `#0099b0` · CLINCH `#e64a19` · GROUND `#9085e9` | passes every check. Don't copy the Annotate timeline's CLINCH orange + GROUND red — they're hard to tell apart even with full colour vision, and that red is also the red corner |
626	| De-emphasis | slate `#94a3b8` | context series: precision/recall lines, "other" |
627	| Span kinds | round `#a3c900` · corner swap `#7c3aed` · excluded `#64748b` | same as the Annotate timeline |
628	| Status | good `#0ca30c` · warning `#fab219` · critical `#ef4444` · unverified `#94a3b8` · not measured `#64748b` | reserved meaning, never a series colour. **Always icon + text** (`check_circle`, `warning`, `error`, `help`, `remove`): good and critical collapse for red-green colour-blind readers, and critical is nearly the same red as the red corner |
629	
630	**Text** wears text tokens (`#f1f5f9`, `#cbd5e1`), never a series colour.
631	`#475569` (text-disabled) is 2.5:1 on the card surface — never use it for data.
632	`#64748b` (text-muted) is 4.0:1 — hints and captions only.
633	
634	**Chart marks:** bars ≤ 24 px thick (8–10 px in dense lists, like the Player's
635	segmented bar), 4 px rounded data end, square at the baseline · 2 px
636	surface-coloured gap between stacked segments · 2 px lines · markers ≥ 8 px with
637	a 2 px surface ring · solid hairline gridlines one step off the surface · one
638	y-axis per chart · a legend whenever there are two or more series, with direct
639	labels only where they fit · a `Table` toggle on every chart showing the same
640	numbers.
641	
642	**Figures:** large standalone numbers use proportional digits; table columns and
643	axis ticks use tabular digits. Compact large counts (`12.9K`).
644	
645	**Avoid** rings or gauges for every metric — a wall of them reads as a sports
646	scoreboard, not an engineering instrument. A meter shows a value against a target;
647	a stat tile shows a single number.
648	
649	## 15. States, interactions, responsive
650	
651	**States** — design each wherever it applies:
652	
653	- **Loading** — skeleton on first load only; a refetch holds the previous render
654	  at reduced opacity.
655	- **Empty** — no labelled fights: "Upload a fight in Manual mode to start
656	  labelling" and the Upload button.
657	- **In progress** — real numbers with an `In progress` tag.
658	- **Not measurable** — see E0.
659	- **Unverified / low evidence** — see C1 and F2.
660	- **Stale** — exported JSON older than the database.
661	- **Error** — backend unreachable: keep the last data, with a banner naming the
662	  last successful refresh time.
663	
664	**Interactions**
665	
666	- Tooltips on every mark — value first, label second. Keyboard focus shows the
667	  same content.
668	- An ⓘ popover beside every metric carries its caveat from §3 in one or two
669	  sentences.
670	- Timeline positions, misses, false positives and queue items open
671	  `/fights/:id/annotate?frame=N` or `/fights/:id?frame=N` (a new parameter).
672	- Copy-command buttons copy the exact CLI command with the fight's video path and
673	  show a "Copied" toast.
674	- Filter state lives in the URL, so a view can be shared.
675	
676	**Responsive**
677	
678	- **≥ 1100 px:** hero (5 cols) + tiles (7 cols); B1 in 8 cols beside B2/B3
679	  stacked in 4; ledger and E full width.
680	- **640–1099 px:** one column; heatmaps scroll sideways inside their card; the
681	  ledger moves State marks through Strike F1 into the row expander.
682	- **< 640 px:** summary only — hero, tiles in a 2-column grid, B1 as a list,
683	  ledger as cards, E1 or E0; other sections collapsed.
684	
685	## 16. What to produce
686	
687	1. Desktop, 1440 px, full page, populated with the sample data.
688	2. The same page as it is today: section E in its not-measurable state (E0).
689	3. The fight ledger with DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA expanded.
690	4. The top of the page at ~1024 px and at 390 px.
691	5. A component sheet: status badge (all 5 states), stat tile, hero meter,
692	   lifecycle dots, heatmap cell with the low-sample tick, coverage strip,
693	   action-queue item, `Circular` badge, `Not scorable` value.
694	
695	**Out of scope:** editing labels (Annotate does that) · fighter performance
696	statistics (the Player does that) · buttons that train or tune anything · pie or
697	donut charts for the event mix · dual-axis charts.
698	
699	## Appendix — where each number comes from
700	
701	Not needed for the visual design; here so the build can follow it.
702	
703	| Data | Source | Status |
704	|---|---|---|
705	| Label counts, targets, corners, activity | `label_events` | Available |
706	| Rounds, swaps, excluded, open spans; seeded-unchanged check | `label_spans` compared with `rounds` | Available |
707	| Track, lifecycle, finished marker, segmentation verdict, video check | `fights` (`state`, `labeled_at`, `segmentation_needs_review/_reason`, `reported/decoded_frames`) | Available |
708	| Predictions to score | `fight_events`, `rounds` | Available |
709	| Exported ground truth | `ai/eval/labels/<video>.json` | On disk; needs a read endpoint |
710	| Score and sanity reports with `git_sha`, `constants_sha256`, `tolerance_frames` | `eval.cli score / sanity --json` (e.g. `ai/eval/baselines/*.json`) | Only when run with `--json`; needs a reports folder and an endpoint |
711	| Human ceiling | `ai/eval/labels/<video>.agreement.json` | Not produced yet |
712	| Label-free corner check | `python -m eval.corner_accuracy <id>` | Printed only; needs `--json` |
713	| Assignment path, clean frames, invariant, box drift, timer coverage | pipeline run log | Log only; needs saving per run |
714	| Swap recall | `eval.cli corner-swap-recall` | Printed only; not run yet |
715	| Tolerance floor and ceiling | derivable from labels (floor needs the agreement run) | Not built |
716	| Video on disk, duplicate uploads | filesystem + `fights.video_path` | Derivable in the backend |

# Training Lab — design brief

> **For Claude Design.** Paste this whole file. It describes a new page for the
> Fight.AI web app: a dashboard over hand-labelled training data and the
> pipeline's measured accuracy. Every number under "Sample" is **illustrative** —
> realistic in shape, modelled on the fights in this repo, not a live snapshot.
> The visual language must match the existing app (§14).

## 1. Context

Fight.AI turns MMA fight video into structured events. A Python pipeline detects
both fighters, tracks them, estimates 17-point pose skeletons, assigns red/blue
corners, reads the scoreboard to find rounds, then runs a hand-tuned rule cascade
that emits strikes (`jab_head`, `ground_punch`, …) and fight state
(STRIKING / CLINCH / GROUND).

That rule cascade is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model, which is
blocked on **labelled data**. A human watches a fight in the **Annotate** page and
logs every strike, state change, takedown, round boundary, corner swap and
excluded stretch. The target is **~300 labelled strikes across 2–3 fights**
(~10–15 min of round time) before training; ~50 is already useful for evaluation.

A labelled fight becomes one of two things, never both:

- **Training fight** — its labels and skeletons feed the model.
- **Evaluation fixture** — it is re-run through the full AI pipeline and the
  predictions are scored against the labels (strike precision/recall/F1, fight
  state, rounds).

Today all of this lives in CLI output (`python -m eval.cli summary | score |
sanity`). The Training Lab puts it on one page.

## 2. Users and the questions the page answers

Users: 1–3 pipeline developers who label fights and change the pipeline.
Technical, data-literate, rightly suspicious of any unqualified number.
Desktop-first.

In priority order, the page must answer:

1. **How much labelled data do we have, of which kinds, and how far are we from
   the 300-strike target?**
2. **Is it trainable?** Which classes are starved? Is one fight dominating?
3. **What is the pipeline's current accuracy — and how far can that number be
   trusted?**
4. **Did the last pipeline change help or hurt?** Against the frozen baseline and
   the previous version.
5. **Is the ground truth itself healthy?** Rounds confirmed, swaps marked, no open
   spans, source video still on disk, exported to git.
6. **What should I do next?** Finish labelling X, export Y, re-run Z as a fixture,
   fix a failing check.

**10-second test:** someone opening the page cold can say "213 of 300 strikes,
ground punches dominate, strike F1 isn't measurable yet because no labelled fight
has predictions."

## 3. Honesty rules — design these in, they are the point of the page

This project has been misled repeatedly by numbers that looked fine. Each rule
matches a real trap in this codebase.

1. **Every metric shows its n and its provenance.** F1 always travels with the
   ground-truth strike count, the fixture count, the matching tolerance
   (±0.25 s = ±12 frames at 50 fps) and the pipeline version (short git SHA +
   constants hash). No bare percentages.
2. **"Not measured", "Not scorable" and "Unverified" are first-class states —
   never 0%, never blank.** A labelled fight processed on the manual track has no
   predictions: its F1 is *not scorable*, not 0%.
3. **Circular metrics are visibly flagged, or hidden.**
   - *Corner read-back* (the labeller's corner matches the pipeline's on matched
     strikes) reads ~100% by construction: the labeller clicks the overlay box the
     pipeline drew, so a tracker swap is copied into the label. Never call it
     "attribution accuracy". It sits behind a `Circular` badge.
   - *Round IoU* is circular when the labelled round spans were auto-seeded from
     the pipeline's own output and never edited. Show `Seeded — not verified`
     instead of an IoU.
4. **Lower bounds say so.** Corner-swap coverage (share of round time inside
   labeller-marked swap spans) is a *lower bound* on corner-assignment error until
   labeller swap recall is measured. Render it as `≥ 4.4%`.
5. **Low evidence is not a pass.** A label-free corner check with few decisive
   frames is `Unverified`, even when it reads 100%.
6. **Accuracy is shown against the human ceiling.** With a double-labelling
   agreement measurement: `F1 56.7% · human ceiling 91.4%`. Without one:
   `ceiling not measured`. An F1 with no ceiling can't be judged good or bad.
7. **Fight state leads with stability, not per-frame accuracy.** Per-frame
   accuracy is dominated by the most common state and stays high while the state
   machine visibly flaps. Lead with transitions/min and median dwell, truth vs
   predicted.
8. **Numbers are only comparable at the same tolerance and on the same fixture
   set.** A trend line breaks (gap plus a note) wherever either changes.

## 4. Placement and layout

- **Nav:** add **Lab** to the header after Analysis and Library (the app already
  uses "Lab Report" wording). Route `/lab`. Page title "Training Lab", subtitle
  "Labelled data and pipeline accuracy".
- **Width:** max 1440 px, centred, 22 px / 30 px page padding — same as the Player.
- **One scrolling page**, with a compact sticky section index on wide screens:
  1. Filter row
  2. **A** Overview
  3. **B** Annotated events
  4. **C** Spans & coverage
  5. **D** Fight ledger
  6. **E** Pipeline accuracy
  7. **F** Pipeline health (label-free)
  8. **G** Label quality & action queue
  - A reference drawer (taxonomy mapping, §13) opens from section B's header.
- **Grid:** 12 columns, 14 px gaps. Every section is a glass card (§14).

## 5. Filter row

One left-aligned row under the page title. It scopes everything below it.

- **Fights:** pills `All labelled` · `Training` · `Evaluation fixtures` ·
  `In progress`, plus a multi-select fight combobox.
- **Labelling period:** `All time` · `Last 7 days` · `Last 30 days`. Affects the
  activity chart and the "added" deltas only.
- **Pipeline version** (scopes E and F): dropdown of scored versions, newest first,
  rows like `807c1b6 · constants a41f… · 10 Sep`; `Working tree (uncommitted)`
  flagged with a dot.
- Far right: `Refreshed 2 min ago` and a refresh icon button. A refetch keeps the
  previous render at reduced opacity — no skeleton flash, no layout jump.

## 6. A · Overview

One **hero card** and a row of stat tiles. The hero is training-set progress — the
user's first question. Accuracy is the most prominent tile, with detail in E.

**Hero card — Training set progress** (~5 columns)

- Hero figure **213 / 300 strikes**, in the app's stat face.
- A meter beneath it: fill = strikes labelled, track = a lighter step of the same
  hue. Ticks at **50** ("useful for evaluation") and **300** ("training target").
- `71% · 87 to go · ~26 days at the last-14-day pace (3.4 strikes/day)`
- `18.4 min of labelled round time across 3 fights`

**Stat tiles**

| Tile | Sample value | Sub-line |
|---|---|---|
| Label events | 250 | +59 in the last 14 days · includes state marks |
| Fights | 3 labelled | 2 finished · 1 in progress · 1 exported to git |
| Largest-fight share | 67% | DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA — warning above 50%: the model would mostly learn one bout |
| Strike detection F1 | `Not scorable` | "No evaluation fixture yet" · populated: `56.7%` · P 62.9 · R 51.7 · n = 118 · ceiling not measured |
| Sanity checks | 7 / 9 | latest AI run · JURIC vs NOGUEIRA |

Clicking a tile scrolls to its section.

## 7. B · Annotated events — "what have we labelled?"

## 11. F · Pipeline health — label-free, works on every processed fight

These checks need no labels. They catch output that is *internally impossible*,
not merely inaccurate, so they run on every AI-processed fight. The corner and
segmentation parts also apply to manual-track fights, which run every stage
except strike detection and the state machine.

### F1. Sanity checks

**Form:** a matrix. Rows = processed fights, columns = the 9 checks, cells = a
status icon: `Pass` · `Fail` · `Not evaluated` (e.g. "no state transitions to
evaluate"). Hover shows the measured value, the detail and the expected band. A
summary column reads `7 / 9`. A `Compare with previous version` toggle adds a
small arrow badge to every cell that changed — flipped to pass (good) or to fail
(critical).

| Check | Expected band |
|---|---|
| Events inside rounds | 0% of strikes outside a round |
| No simultaneous mutual strikes | ≤ 2% of events |
| No duplicate events | 0 |
| State does not flap | ≤ 15 transitions/min |
| State dwell is physical | median ≥ 1.0 s |
| Strike rate is plausible | 5–60 strikes/min |
| No short interior rounds | 0 |
| Round breaks are real breaks | 0 gaps too short |
| Round count fits video length | ≤ what the video can hold |

Sample history (these are the real committed baseline reports for JURIC vs
NOGUEIRA):

- `769e83f` — 2 of 6 pass: mutual strikes 75% ✕, duplicate events 4 ✕,
  19.6 transitions/min ✕, dwell 0.76 s ✕. The 3 round checks didn't exist yet —
  `Not evaluated`.
- `5ecd0ba` — 3 of 4 pass: strike rate 3.1/min ✕. State checks `Not evaluated`
  (no transitions); round checks `Not evaluated`.

### F2. Corner assignment (per fight)

- **Label-free corner check** — `95% correct · 219 decisive frames` → `OK`.
  Below 90% → `Intermittent swaps` (warning). Below 50% → `Inverted` (critical).
  Fewer decisive frames than a minimum (proposed default 30) → `Unverified`,
  whatever the percentage. A thin strip along the fight's timeline shows OK and
  flipped runs, plus the gaps where no frame was decisive (typically ground
  sequences).
- **Assignment path** — `Appearance` · `Legacy fallback — ambiguous tape (both
  slots read blue)` · `Legacy fallback — too few clean frames`.
- **Clean frames per slot** — `412 / 388`.
- **Duplicate-corner invariant** — `OK` or `Violated` (critical: a release
  blocker).
- **Box/skeleton drift** — `0.62% of rows` (the skeleton's torso centre falls
  outside its own box).

Sample: JURIC vs NOGUEIRA `100% · 17 fr → Unverified` · MILIDRAGOVIC vs MOOSMAN
`93% · 86 fr → OK` · NAZHAND vs STAROPOLI `95% · 219 fr → OK` · DRAGOJEVIC vs
HONDA `58% · 55 fr → Intermittent swaps`.

### F3. Segmentation and source video

- **Round source** — `Clock` (scoreboard timer fitted) or `Detection only`
  (warning: "boundaries are a guess"), timer coverage %, round-number coverage %,
  and the pipeline's review reason verbatim.
- **Video integrity** — `reported 35,589 · decoded 35,589 frames ✓` and
  `File on disk ✓ / ✕`. Tooltip: "Labels point at frames of this exact file. A
  missing or re-encoded video detaches every label."

## 12. G · Label quality & action queue

### G1. Can we trust the labels?

Three status cards:

- **Human agreement ceiling** — `Not measured`. "Label one round twice — a second
  person, or yourself a week later — to get a ceiling for every F1." Once
  measured: detection F1, family agreement, corner agreement (expect ~100%; lower
  means a labelling-UI defect) and the most common disagreements.
- **Corner-swap recall** — `Not run`. "Inject a known swap, label the fight
  normally, check the swap got marked." Once run: detected or missed, plus start
  and end edge error in frames.
- **Matching tolerance** — `±0.25 s, pinned`. A range bar from a floor (p95 of
  human timing jitter — needs the agreement run) to a ceiling (p5 of the gap
  between one fighter's consecutive strikes — computable from labels today), with
  the current value marked. Critical when the current value is above the ceiling:
  "fast combinations can shift-match and inflate F1". Sample ceiling: 0.18 s →
  critical.

### G2. Action queue

A prioritised list grouped by severity. Each item: status icon + label, fight,
a one-line explanation, one action (`Open at frame` · `Copy command` ·
`Snooze 7 days`).

- **Critical:** same bout used for training and evaluation · duplicate-corner
  invariant violated · tolerance above the combination ceiling · source video
  missing for a labelled fight
- **Warning:** open span (export skips it) · strikes outside every round span
  (dropped on export) · state mark with a corner attached · labels after the
  fight-end mark · finished but not exported · export older than the latest
  labels · round span seeded and never adjusted · segmentation needs review · low
  label density on a finished fight · one fight above 50% of strikes · class below
  the minimum · corner check unverified or intermittent · failing sanity check
- **Info:** events captured but not exported (takedown attempt/defended,
  submission, knockdown, fight end) · no labeller name · human ceiling not

  gradient primary button for at most one action per view.
- **Motion:** sections fade up on first load (0.5 s, staggered 80 ms). Nothing
  animates on refetch.

**Colour roles** — checked with a palette validator against the card surface
(≈ `#0f1113`), including simulated colour blindness:

| Role | Colours | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Magnitude — bars, heatmaps, meters | cyan ramp from `#00daf3` | one hue; nominal categories never get a colour each |
| Corner | red `#ff4d4d` · blue `#3aa0ff` | clearly separable for all readers; always paired with an R/B label or the fighter's name |
| Fight state (charts on this page) | STRIKING `#0099b0` · CLINCH `#e64a19` · GROUND `#9085e9` | passes every check. Don't copy the Annotate timeline's CLINCH orange + GROUND red — they're hard to tell apart even with full colour vision, and that red is also the red corner |
| De-emphasis | slate `#94a3b8` | context series: precision/recall lines, "other" |
| Span kinds | round `#a3c900` · corner swap `#7c3aed` · excluded `#64748b` | same as the Annotate timeline |
| Status | good `#0ca30c` · warning `#fab219` · critical `#ef4444` · unverified `#94a3b8` · not measured `#64748b` | reserved meaning, never a series colour. **Always icon + text** (`check_circle`, `warning`, `error`, `help`, `remove`): good and critical collapse for red-green colour-blind readers, and critical is nearly the same red as the red corner |

**Text** wears text tokens (`#f1f5f9`, `#cbd5e1`), never a series colour.
`#475569` (text-disabled) is 2.5:1 on the card surface — never use it for data.
`#64748b` (text-muted) is 4.0:1 — hints and captions only.

**Chart marks:** bars ≤ 24 px thick (8–10 px in dense lists, like the Player's
segmented bar), 4 px rounded data end, square at the baseline · 2 px
surface-coloured gap between stacked segments · 2 px lines · markers ≥ 8 px with
a 2 px surface ring · solid hairline gridlines one step off the surface · one
y-axis per chart · a legend whenever there are two or more series, with direct
labels only where they fit · a `Table` toggle on every chart showing the same
numbers.

**Figures:** large standalone numbers use proportional digits; table columns and
axis ticks use tabular digits. Compact large counts (`12.9K`).

**Avoid** rings or gauges for every metric — a wall of them reads as a sports
scoreboard, not an engineering instrument. A meter shows a value against a target;
a stat tile shows a single number.

## 15. States, interactions, responsive

**States** — design each wherever it applies:

- **Loading** — skeleton on first load only; a refetch holds the previous render
  at reduced opacity.
- **Empty** — no labelled fights: "Upload a fight in Manual mode to start
  labelling" and the Upload button.
- **In progress** — real numbers with an `In progress` tag.
- **Not measurable** — see E0.
- **Unverified / low evidence** — see C1 and F2.
- **Stale** — exported JSON older than the database.
- **Error** — backend unreachable: keep the last data, with a banner naming the
  last successful refresh time.

**Interactions**

- Tooltips on every mark — value first, label second. Keyboard focus shows the
  same content.
- An ⓘ popover beside every metric carries its caveat from §3 in one or two
  sentences.
- Timeline positions, misses, false positives and queue items open
  `/fights/:id/annotate?frame=N` or `/fights/:id?frame=N` (a new parameter).
- Copy-command buttons copy the exact CLI command with the fight's video path and
  show a "Copied" toast.
- Filter state lives in the URL, so a view can be shared.

**Responsive**

- **≥ 1100 px:** hero (5 cols) + tiles (7 cols); B1 in 8 cols beside B2/B3
  stacked in 4; ledger and E full width.
- **640–1099 px:** one column; heatmaps scroll sideways inside their card; the
  ledger moves State marks through Strike F1 into the row expander.
- **< 640 px:** summary only — hero, tiles in a 2-column grid, B1 as a list,
  ledger as cards, E1 or E0; other sections collapsed.

## 16. What to produce

1. Desktop, 1440 px, full page, populated with the sample data.
2. The same page as it is today: section E in its not-measurable state (E0).
3. The fight ledger with DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA expanded.
4. The top of the page at ~1024 px and at 390 px.
5. A component sheet: status badge (all 5 states), stat tile, hero meter,
   lifecycle dots, heatmap cell with the low-sample tick, coverage strip,
   action-queue item, `Circular` badge, `Not scorable` value.

**Out of scope:** editing labels (Annotate does that) · fighter performance
statistics (the Player does that) · buttons that train or tune anything · pie or
donut charts for the event mix · dual-axis charts.

## Appendix — where each number comes from

Not needed for the visual design; here so the build can follow it.

| Data | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Label counts, targets, corners, activity | `label_events` | Available |
| Rounds, swaps, excluded, open spans; seeded-unchanged check | `label_spans` compared with `rounds` | Available |
| Track, lifecycle, finished marker, segmentation verdict, video check | `fights` (`state`, `labeled_at`, `segmentation_needs_review/_reason`, `reported/decoded_frames`) | Available |
| Predictions to score | `fight_events`, `rounds` | Available |
| Exported ground truth | `ai/eval/labels/<video>.json` | On disk; needs a read endpoint |
| Score and sanity reports with `git_sha`, `constants_sha256`, `tolerance_frames` | `eval.cli score / sanity --json` (e.g. `ai/eval/baselines/*.json`) | Only when run with `--json`; needs a reports folder and an endpoint |
| Human ceiling | `ai/eval/labels/<video>.agreement.json` | Not produced yet |
| Label-free corner check | `python -m eval.corner_accuracy <id>` | Printed only; needs `--json` |
| Assignment path, clean frames, invariant, box drift, timer coverage | pipeline run log | Log only; needs saving per run |
| Swap recall | `eval.cli corner-swap-recall` | Printed only; not run yet |
| Tolerance floor and ceiling | derivable from labels (floor needs the agreement run) | Not built |
| Video on disk, duplicate uploads | filesystem + `fights.video_path` | Derivable in the backend |

# Fight AI — Frontend

## Workflow
- Always apply changes directly to the local working directory
- Never open PRs or suggest creating pull requests

## What it does
React + TypeScript + Vite app for reviewing processed MMA fight videos. Displays fight events in a live feed, shows DB-backed round information, and renders toggleable fighter bounding-box overlays on the video.

## Project Structure
```

├── types/
│   ├── Event.ts          # ONE shape for both pipeline predictions and hand labels,
│   │                      #   told apart by `source`/`kind`: { id, fight_id, source
│   │                      #   ('prediction'|'label'), kind ('point'|'round'|
│   │                      #   'corner_swap'|'excluded'), frame, end_frame (null
│   │                      #   for kind='point'), description (null except for
│   │                      #   action='fight_end' — see utils/describeEvent.ts),
│   │                      #   fighter_id (prediction-only), corner
│   │                      #   (label-only, 0=red/1=blue — a track-slot, not a
│   │                      #   resolved person), action, target, success, state
│   │                      #   (prediction-only), value (range-kind-only),
│   │                      #   labeler, created_at }
