│   │                      #   segmentation_needs_review/_reason, red/blue_fighter_id }
│   │                      #   + STATE_LABELS/STATE_PROGRESS/TERMINAL_STATES maps,
│   │                      #   FightPurpose + PURPOSE_LABELS/_COLORS/_ICONS, and
│   │                      #   isFightViewable/isLabelingReady/isInvalid/needsRoundReview
│   │                      #   predicates

├── services/
│   └── api.ts            # fetchEvents(fightId, params) (source/kind/fighter_id/action/
│                          #   success filters), createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent
│                          #   (Annotate's write path — always source='label' server-side),
│                          #   fetchFights, fetchFighterFrames, fetchRounds, uploadFight,
│                          #   deleteFight, finishLabeling
├── hooks/

│   │                      #   fighter_id, action, success} params, exposes a setter for

│   │                      #   Annotate passes {source:'label'} and derives its own

├── utils/
│   ├── describeEvent.ts  # Reconstructs an Event's display text on demand (description is
│   │                     #   only ever stored for action='fight_end') from action/target/
│   │                     #   corner (labels, via annotate/taxonomy.ts's ToolItem.text()
│   │                     #   templates) or action/fighter_id/success/state + `rounds`
│   │                     #   (predictions) — used by both LiveFeed and AnnotationList/Timeline
│   ├── eventTaxonomy.ts  # categoryForAction/colorForAction/iconForAction — action-driven,
│   │                     #   shared by LiveFeed (Player) and annotate/taxonomy.ts (re-exports
│   │                     #   these for its existing importers)
│   ├── cornerSwap.ts     # isFrameSwapped(frame, spans) — shared by FighterOverlay (box/
│   │                     #   skeleton colour) and describeEvent (fighter-name resolution)
│   └── liveStats.ts      # deriveStatsForRange/derivePaceBuckets — FIGHT STATISTICS/MOMENTUM,
│                         #   attributes strikes via fighter_id (predictions, vs. fights.
│                         #   red_fighter_id) or corner (labels), never via description text
├── components/
│   ├── FighterOverlay.tsx  # canvas overlay for fighter bounding boxes
│   ├── VideoPlayer.tsx     # <video> wrapper with play/seek gestures; accepts children for overlays
│   ├── VideoControls.tsx   # playback controls + scrubber
│   ├── FrameInfo.tsx       # frame / ms / fps display
│   ├── Header.tsx          # top nav
│   ├── CornerSelect.tsx    # fighter search/create combobox, used by the upload dialog
│   ├── FightPurposeBadge.tsx # training_data/reference/ai_labeled chip — fight list
│   │                       #   subtitle + Player and Annotate headers
│   ├── ConfirmDialog.tsx   # reusable confirm modal (title/message/danger/busy/error);
│   │                       #   backs fight deletion from both Player and FightList
│   ├── annotate/           # Annotate page sub-components — see "Labelling (Annotate page)" below
│   │   ├── taxonomy.ts         # ToolItem palette definitions, KEYMAP, colour/icon/category

│   │   ├── AnnotationPanel.tsx # timeline/list view toggle + filter pills, wraps the two below
│   │   ├── AnnotationTimeline.tsx # multi-lane timeline: rounds, state segs, corner_swap/
│   │   │                       #   excluded spans (draggable edges), red/blue strike clips
│   │   ├── AnnotationList.tsx  # flat chronological list view of label events
│   │   └── SaveStatus.tsx      # small "saving…" indicator (savingCount > 0)
│   └── player/             # Analysis Player sub-components
│       ├── LiveFeed.tsx    # real-event chat feed with filter pills + click-to-seek —
│       │                   #   text via utils/describeEvent.ts, category/colour/icon via
│       │                   #   utils/eventTaxonomy.ts (no more regex-over-description)
│       ├── ScopeToggle.tsx # Whole Fight / Round 1 / Round 2 pill group
│       ├── AccGauge.tsx    # SVG accuracy ring gauge
│       ├── SegBar.tsx      # horizontal segmented bar (strikes by target / position)
│       ├── PaceChart.tsx   # SVG area/line pace chart with live playhead
│       ├── MiniStat.tsx    # small inner-tile stat (Takedowns, Control, KD, Sub Att)
│       ├── EdgeMeter.tsx   # tale-of-the-tape needle (Height / Reach / Age)
│       ├── RecentForm.tsx  # W/L chip list (Recent Form · Last 5)
│       ├── FighterColumn.tsx  # per-fighter stats card (AccGauge + MiniStat + SegBar)
│       ├── FightStatistics.tsx # scope bar + ScopeToggle + two FighterColumn
│       ├── Momentum.tsx    # MOMENTUM card wrapping PaceChart
│       └── MatchupCard.tsx # tale-of-the-tape + EdgeMeter rows + RecentForm
└── pages/
    ├── Player.tsx          # main fight-review page (Analysis Player redesign) — reads predictions
    ├── Annotate.tsx        # manual-labelling page — reads/writes fight_events rows with source='label'
    ├── FightList.tsx       # fight library / upload entry point, live via useFightStream
    └── Library.tsx         # legacy fight library listing
```

## Analysis Player Layout

`Player.tsx` implements a cinematic, full-page layout with five stacked sections (top → bottom):

1. **Top grid** (`1fr 410px`, collapses single-column below 1100px) — `<VideoPlayer>` + `FighterOverlay` + ROUND chip on the left; `LiveFeed` filling the right column via absolute positioning so it always matches the video column height.
2. **FIGHT STATISTICS** — `FightStatistics.tsx`: glass bar with `monitoring` icon + `ScopeToggle` (Whole Fight / Round 1 / Round 2); two `FighterColumn` cards below (real scope state selects the mock stat set from `fightMock.ts`).
3. **MOMENTUM** — `Momentum.tsx`: `PaceChart` (SVG area/line, mock pace data, real time-axis from `currentTime`/`duration`; real `r1EndSeconds` from `useRounds` or fallback mock).
4. **MATCHUP** — `MatchupCard.tsx`: tale-of-the-tape header + `EdgeRow` needles for Height/Reach/Age + Recent Form W/L chips.

### Live feed event derivation
`LiveFeed` drives on **real** backend events (same `useEvents` hook) — `{ source: 'prediction' }` for an `ai_labeled` fight, `{ source: 'label' }` otherwise (a fight is never re-run, so exactly one source ever has real content — see "Fight purpose" below). Each event's category/colour/icon come from `utils/eventTaxonomy.ts`'s `categoryForAction`/`colorForAction`/`iconForAction`, driven entirely by the structured `action` column; its display text comes from `utils/describeEvent.ts`, reconstructed from `action`/`target`/`corner` (labels) or `action`/`fighter_id`/`success`/`state` (predictions) — never from `description`, which is only ever stored for `action='fight_end'`. `LiveFeed` is passed `redName`/`blueName`, `redFighterId` (`fights.red_fighter_id`, to resolve a prediction's `fighter_id`), `rounds` (to recover a round marker's number), and `cornerSwapSpans` (to swap-correct a label event's fighter name for its own frame, independent of the current playhead). Filter pills (All / Strikes / Fight State / Grapple) and click-to-seek work the same way as the design reference.

### Mock data
All hardcoded values (fighter profiles, per-round stats, pace arrays, recent form) live in `src/mocks/fightMock.ts`. Every gap is documented with the API shape needed to replace it in `TODO_BACKEND_DATA.md`.

### Responsive
`useWindowWidth()` drives a `narrow = width < 1100` flag. Below 1100px: top grid collapses to single column (live feed becomes a fixed-height `420px` block below controls); fighter columns stack; matchup tale-of-the-tape collapses; form lists both align left.

## API Proxy (vite.config.ts)
Both `/events` and `/fights` are proxied to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
Video files are served from `public/` via a custom range-request middleware.

## Frame-numbering contract
**Frames are 1-based** — the first frame of the video is frame 1.

Convert `video.currentTime` to a frame number with:
```ts
const currentFrame = Math.floor(currentTime * fps) + 1;
```
where `fps` comes from `FightResponse.fps` (an integer stored on the `fights` DB row).

This value is used to:
- Look up `frameMap.get(currentFrame)` in `FighterOverlay`
- Filter `events.filter(e => e.frame <= currentFrame)` in `Player`
- Match round boundaries: `rounds.find(r => currentFrame >= r.start_frame && currentFrame <= r.end_frame)`

Never hardcode an fps value — always use `selectedFight.fps`.

## FighterOverlay component
`<canvas>` absolutely positioned over the video (`pointer-events: none`).

On each `currentFrame` change:
1. Resize canvas to its CSS display size (`canvas.width = canvas.clientWidth`, etc.)
2. Clear canvas
3. If `showBoxes` is false, return early
4. Look up `frameMap.get(currentFrame)` → array of `FighterFrame`
5. Scale each bbox from the fight's **native resolution** (`fightWidth` × `fightHeight` from `FightResponse`) to the canvas display size:
   ```ts
   const scaleX = canvas.width / fightWidth;
   const scaleY = canvas.height / fightHeight;
   ```
6. Draw red rect for `corner === 0`, blue for `corner === 1` — **flipped** if the frame falls inside a `cornerSwapSpans` entry (`utils/cornerSwap.ts`'s `isFrameSwapped`), a display-only correction for a confirmed `corner_swap` label span. `fighter_frames.corner` itself is never touched — see `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person`.

`VideoPlayer` accepts `children` so `FighterOverlay` can be rendered inside the `position: relative` video container and stack correctly.

## Fight selector (Player.tsx)
- Populated from `useFights`, filtered to `isFightViewable(state)` (`completed` or `labeling_complete`)
- Defaults to the most recently processed fight (last element of the list)
- Changing selection re-fetches events, frames, and rounds for the new fight

## Fight purpose

`Fight.purpose` says what a video is *for*: `training_data` (labels feed model training),
`reference` (held out of training; scored against to measure pipeline accuracy) or
`ai_labeled` (produced by the full AI pipeline). It is chosen in `UploadDialog` and set
once server-side at upload — nothing can change it afterwards, and a fight's pipeline
never runs again after that first pass. Pipeline accuracy is validated by uploading
the *same* source video a second time as a brand-new fight (`purpose='ai_labeled'`,
a different fight_id) and comparing its predictions against the first upload's hand
labels across the two fight IDs — not by re-processing an already-labelled fight.

`UploadDialog` derives it from the two `ModeCard`s: **AI annotation** forces
`ai_labeled` (not user-selectable), **Self-annotate** reveals a radio row —
native `<input type="radio" name="fight-purpose">`, the only radio group in the app —
with **no default selected**, and the submit button stays disabled until one is picked.
That gate is deliberate: training and evaluation sets must stay disjoint, so the split
should never be decided by inattention. `uploadFight()` sends `purpose` as the sole
track selector; the old `mode: 'ai' | 'manual'` form field is gone, since `purpose`
already implies it.

`FightPurposeBadge` renders the chip. Its colours (`PURPOSE_COLORS` in `Fight.ts`)
deliberately avoid the corner colours `#ff4d4d`/`#3aa0ff` — a badge in either would read
as "red corner" — plus `#ef4444` (error) and `#f59e0b` (the rounds-unverified warning).

## Deleting a fight
`DELETE /fights/{id}` is irreversible — it kills any running pipeline, unlinks the video file, and
cascades away every fight_events row (predictions and hand labels alike), rounds and fighter frames. Two entry points, both
routed through `ConfirmDialog`:

- **`Player.tsx`** — Delete button in the back-nav row (icon-only when `narrow`). The only way to
  delete a healthy fight. Two things the handler must keep doing: `videoRef.current.pause()` before
  the request, because the DELETE unlinks the file the `<video>` is streaming and the
  `requestVideoFrameCallback` loop is still reading it; and `navigate('/', { replace: true })`, so
  browser Back can't land on a now-dead `/fights/{id}`.
- **`Annotate.tsx`** — icon-only button at the far right of the header, past "Finish Labeling".
  Its `confirmDelete` state is mirrored into `confirmDeleteRef` and checked in the global keydown
  handler alongside `endOpenRef` — **any new modal on this page must do the same**, or its overlay
  will happily sit there while `z`/`o`/`p`/digit presses keep writing label events and spans
  underneath it.
- **`FightList.tsx`** — gated behind `errored` (`failed || invalid`), so it does *not* appear on
  healthy cards; it's a "delete and re-upload" recovery affordance, not a general delete. One
  dialog instance lives outside the `.map`, driven by `pendingDelete`.

Set `KEEP_VIDEO_ON_DELETE=1` on the backend when exercising this by hand — the row still goes, but
the source video survives.

## Key design decisions
- `useFighterFrames` builds a `Map<number, FighterFrame[]>` on load for O(1) per-frame overlay lookup during playback
- `useRounds` provides DB-backed round boundaries; `Player` uses `rounds.find(...)` instead of a hardcoded duration constant
- `stepFrame(delta)` uses `delta / fps` seconds, so frame-stepping is always exact regardless of the video's actual fps

## Labelling (Annotate page)

`Annotate.tsx` (`/fights/{id}/annotate`) is where a **manual**-mode upload gets hand-labelled once it reaches `labeling_in_progress`. It shares `AnnotateStage`/`VideoPlayer`/`FighterOverlay` with the Player, and calls the same `useEvents`/`GET /fights/{id}/events/` as the Player does — but always with `{ source: 'label' }`, and it only ever creates/updates/deletes through `createEvent`/`updateEvent`/`deleteEvent`, which the backend always writes as `source='label'`. The backend enforces the other half: `event_service.delete_event`/`update_event` are scoped to `source='label'` rows only, so nothing Annotate does can ever touch a `source='prediction'` row, even though both now live in one `fight_events` table.

**Palette-driven strikes/state/etc. (`taxonomy.ts` → `createEvent({ kind: 'point', ... })`).** Every `ToolItem` in `TOOL_GROUPS` drives its palette button, keyboard shortcut, and the keyboard legend from one definition. Hand strikes (jab/hooks/uppercuts/elbow) carry `hasTarget: true` — plain key = head, `Shift`+key = body, read via `e.code` (not `e.key`, which a US layout maps to a different character under Shift) together with `e.shiftKey`. Kicks carry a `fixedTarget` instead (the action name already encodes it: `calf_kick`/`low_kick` → leg, `middle_kick` → body, `high_kick` → head). `successForAction` returns `null` for every strike except `knockdown` — landed-vs-missed is deferred, so nothing claims a strike landed by default. `logTool()` no longer sends a `description` in the create payload for any of these — `ToolItem.text()` is only used locally to build the toast message; the stored row carries `action`/`target`/`corner` and its display text is reconstructed on every render by `utils/describeEvent.ts` (`ACTION_TO_TOOL`, a reverse index over `TOOL_GROUPS`, is what that reconstruction looks the `ToolItem` back up by). `fight_end` (built ad hoc in `confirmFightEnd`, not a `ToolItem`) is the one action that still sends and stores a real `description`.

`Annotate.tsx` builds one `describe(e)` closure (over `redName`/`blueName` and the fight's own `corner_swap` spans, via `utils/describeEvent.ts` + `isFrameSwapped`) and passes it down through `AnnotationPanel` to both `AnnotationList` and `AnnotationTimeline`, which call it instead of reading `e.description` anywhere (list rows, timeline clip titles, the hover tooltip) — so marking or editing a `corner_swap` span updates already-logged strikes' displayed fighter name immediately, with no backfill.

**Span annotation (`O`/`P` keys → `createEvent({ kind: 'round'|'corner_swap'|'excluded', ... })`).** `round`/`corner_swap`/`excluded` rows are the range-shaped `kind`s of the same `fight_events` table (`frame` = start, `end_frame` nullable). `round` events are auto-seeded server-side from the AI-segmented `rounds` table the first time Annotate fetches `source='label'` events for a fight, and rendered as draggable blocks in `AnnotationTimeline`'s ROUNDS lane (edge-drag calls `onUpdateSpan`, which `PUT`s `frame`/`end_frame`). `corner_swap`/`excluded` are start/end toggles: `Annotate.tsx`'s `openSpanRef` tracks the in-flight event id per kind so the second `O`/`P` press knows what to close — `toggleSpan()` creates one with `end_frame=null` on open, `PUT`s `end_frame` to close it. `AnnotationTimeline` renders an open span dashed, running to the current playhead. `Annotate.tsx` derives its `events` (kind='point') and `spans` (kind!='point') arrays from the one `useEvents(fightId, { source: 'label' })` result via `useMemo`.

**"Finish Labeling" is gated.** `POST /fights/{id}/finish-labeling` (via `handleFinishLabeling`) 409s until every detected round has a confirmed `round`-kind label event — the backend check (`rounds_fully_annotated`), not anything client-side.

**Fight-state marks are change points, not spans.** `W`/`F`/`G` (STRIKING/CLINCH/GROUND) log a single-frame `label_event`; `AnnotationTimeline`'s STATE lane derives contiguous segments by pairing each mark with the next one chronologically (last mark implicitly runs to the end of the timeline in the UI — the harness-side derivation in `ai/eval/labels_db.py` instead runs it to the end of its round, which matters when exporting).

```

## Analysis Player Layout

`Player.tsx` implements a cinematic, full-page layout with five stacked sections (top → bottom):

1. **Top grid** (`1fr 410px`, collapses single-column below 1100px) — `<VideoPlayer>` + `FighterOverlay` + ROUND chip on the left; `LiveFeed` filling the right column via absolute positioning so it always matches the video column height.
2. **FIGHT STATISTICS** — `FightStatistics.tsx`: glass bar with `monitoring` icon + `ScopeToggle` (Whole Fight / Round 1 / Round 2); two `FighterColumn` cards below (real scope state selects the mock stat set from `fightMock.ts`).
3. **MOMENTUM** — `Momentum.tsx`: `PaceChart` (SVG area/line, mock pace data, real time-axis from `currentTime`/`duration`; real `r1EndSeconds` from `useRounds` or fallback mock).
4. **MATCHUP** — `MatchupCard.tsx`: tale-of-the-tape header + `EdgeRow` needles for Height/Reach/Age + Recent Form W/L chips.

### Live feed event derivation
`LiveFeed` drives on **real** backend events (same `useEvents` hook) — `{ source: 'prediction' }` for an `ai_labeled` fight, `{ source: 'label' }` otherwise (a fight is never re-run, so exactly one source ever has real content — see "Fight purpose" below). Each event's category/colour/icon come from `utils/eventTaxonomy.ts`'s `categoryForAction`/`colorForAction`/`iconForAction`, driven entirely by the structured `action` column; its display text comes from `utils/describeEvent.ts`, reconstructed from `action`/`target`/`corner` (labels) or `action`/`fighter_id`/`success`/`state` (predictions) — never from `description`, which is only ever stored for `action='fight_end'`. `LiveFeed` is passed `redName`/`blueName`, `redFighterId` (`fights.red_fighter_id`, to resolve a prediction's `fighter_id`), `rounds` (to recover a round marker's number), and `cornerSwapSpans` (to swap-correct a label event's fighter name for its own frame, independent of the current playhead). Filter pills (All / Strikes / Fight State / Grapple) and click-to-seek work the same way as the design reference.

### Mock data
All hardcoded values (fighter profiles, per-round stats, pace arrays, recent form) live in `src/mocks/fightMock.ts`. Every gap is documented with the API shape needed to replace it in `TODO_BACKEND_DATA.md`.

### Responsive
`useWindowWidth()` drives a `narrow = width < 1100` flag. Below 1100px: top grid collapses to single column (live feed becomes a fixed-height `420px` block below controls); fighter columns stack; matchup tale-of-the-tape collapses; form lists both align left.

## API Proxy (vite.config.ts)
Both `/events` and `/fights` are proxied to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
Video files are served from `public/` via a custom range-request middleware.

## Frame-numbering contract
**Frames are 1-based** — the first frame of the video is frame 1.

Convert `video.currentTime` to a frame number with:
```ts
const currentFrame = Math.floor(currentTime * fps) + 1;
```
where `fps` comes from `FightResponse.fps` (an integer stored on the `fights` DB row).

This value is used to:
- Look up `frameMap.get(currentFrame)` in `FighterOverlay`
- Filter `events.filter(e => e.frame <= currentFrame)` in `Player`
- Match round boundaries: `rounds.find(r => currentFrame >= r.start_frame && currentFrame <= r.end_frame)`

Never hardcode an fps value — always use `selectedFight.fps`.

## FighterOverlay component
`<canvas>` absolutely positioned over the video (`pointer-events: none`).

On each `currentFrame` change:
1. Resize canvas to its CSS display size (`canvas.width = canvas.clientWidth`, etc.)
2. Clear canvas
3. If `showBoxes` is false, return early
4. Look up `frameMap.get(currentFrame)` → array of `FighterFrame`
5. Scale each bbox from the fight's **native resolution** (`fightWidth` × `fightHeight` from `FightResponse`) to the canvas display size:
   ```ts
   const scaleX = canvas.width / fightWidth;
   const scaleY = canvas.height / fightHeight;
   ```
6. Draw red rect for `corner === 0`, blue for `corner === 1` — **flipped** if the frame falls inside a `cornerSwapSpans` entry (`utils/cornerSwap.ts`'s `isFrameSwapped`), a display-only correction for a confirmed `corner_swap` label span. `fighter_frames.corner` itself is never touched — see `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person`.

`VideoPlayer` accepts `children` so `FighterOverlay` can be rendered inside the `position: relative` video container and stack correctly.

## Fight selector (Player.tsx)
- Populated from `useFights`, filtered to `isFightViewable(state)` (`completed` or `labeling_complete`)
- Defaults to the most recently processed fight (last element of the list)
- Changing selection re-fetches events, frames, and rounds for the new fight

## Fight purpose

`Fight.purpose` says what a video is *for*: `training_data` (labels feed model training),
`reference` (held out of training; scored against to measure pipeline accuracy) or
`ai_labeled` (produced by the full AI pipeline). It is chosen in `UploadDialog` and set
once server-side at upload — nothing can change it afterwards, and a fight's pipeline
never runs again after that first pass. Pipeline accuracy is validated by uploading
the *same* source video a second time as a brand-new fight (`purpose='ai_labeled'`,
a different fight_id) and comparing its predictions against the first upload's hand
labels across the two fight IDs — not by re-processing an already-labelled fight.

`UploadDialog` derives it from the two `ModeCard`s: **AI annotation** forces
`ai_labeled` (not user-selectable), **Self-annotate** reveals a radio row —
native `<input type="radio" name="fight-purpose">`, the only radio group in the app —
with **no default selected**, and the submit button stays disabled until one is picked.
That gate is deliberate: training and evaluation sets must stay disjoint, so the split
should never be decided by inattention. `uploadFight()` sends `purpose` as the sole
track selector; the old `mode: 'ai' | 'manual'` form field is gone, since `purpose`
already implies it.

`FightPurposeBadge` renders the chip. Its colours (`PURPOSE_COLORS` in `Fight.ts`)
deliberately avoid the corner colours `#ff4d4d`/`#3aa0ff` — a badge in either would read
as "red corner" — plus `#ef4444` (error) and `#f59e0b` (the rounds-unverified warning).

## Deleting a fight
`DELETE /fights/{id}` is irreversible — it kills any running pipeline, unlinks the video file, and
cascades away every fight_events row (predictions and hand labels alike), rounds and fighter frames. Two entry points, both
routed through `ConfirmDialog`:

- **`Player.tsx`** — Delete button in the back-nav row (icon-only when `narrow`). The only way to
  delete a healthy fight. Two things the handler must keep doing: `videoRef.current.pause()` before
  the request, because the DELETE unlinks the file the `<video>` is streaming and the
  `requestVideoFrameCallback` loop is still reading it; and `navigate('/', { replace: true })`, so
  browser Back can't land on a now-dead `/fights/{id}`.
- **`Annotate.tsx`** — icon-only button at the far right of the header, past "Finish Labeling".
  Its `confirmDelete` state is mirrored into `confirmDeleteRef` and checked in the global keydown
  handler alongside `endOpenRef` — **any new modal on this page must do the same**, or its overlay
  will happily sit there while `z`/`o`/`p`/digit presses keep writing label events and spans
  underneath it.
- **`FightList.tsx`** — gated behind `errored` (`failed || invalid`), so it does *not* appear on
  healthy cards; it's a "delete and re-upload" recovery affordance, not a general delete. One
  dialog instance lives outside the `.map`, driven by `pendingDelete`.

Set `KEEP_VIDEO_ON_DELETE=1` on the backend when exercising this by hand — the row still goes, but
the source video survives.

## Key design decisions
- `useFighterFrames` builds a `Map<number, FighterFrame[]>` on load for O(1) per-frame overlay lookup during playback
- `useRounds` provides DB-backed round boundaries; `Player` uses `rounds.find(...)` instead of a hardcoded duration constant
- `stepFrame(delta)` uses `delta / fps` seconds, so frame-stepping is always exact regardless of the video's actual fps

## Labelling (Annotate page)

`Annotate.tsx` (`/fights/{id}/annotate`) is where a **manual**-mode upload gets hand-labelled once it reaches `labeling_in_progress`. It shares `AnnotateStage`/`VideoPlayer`/`FighterOverlay` with the Player, and calls the same `useEvents`/`GET /fights/{id}/events/` as the Player does — but always with `{ source: 'label' }`, and it only ever creates/updates/deletes through `createEvent`/`updateEvent`/`deleteEvent`, which the backend always writes as `source='label'`. The backend enforces the other half: `event_service.delete_event`/`update_event` are scoped to `source='label'` rows only, so nothing Annotate does can ever touch a `source='prediction'` row, even though both now live in one `fight_events` table.

**Palette-driven strikes/state/etc. (`taxonomy.ts` → `createEvent({ kind: 'point', ... })`).** Every `ToolItem` in `TOOL_GROUPS` drives its palette button, keyboard shortcut, and the keyboard legend from one definition. Hand strikes (jab/hooks/uppercuts/elbow) carry `hasTarget: true` — plain key = head, `Shift`+key = body, read via `e.code` (not `e.key`, which a US layout maps to a different character under Shift) together with `e.shiftKey`. Kicks carry a `fixedTarget` instead (the action name already encodes it: `calf_kick`/`low_kick` → leg, `middle_kick` → body, `high_kick` → head). `successForAction` returns `null` for every strike except `knockdown` — landed-vs-missed is deferred, so nothing claims a strike landed by default. `logTool()` no longer sends a `description` in the create payload for any of these — `ToolItem.text()` is only used locally to build the toast message; the stored row carries `action`/`target`/`corner` and its display text is reconstructed on every render by `utils/describeEvent.ts` (`ACTION_TO_TOOL`, a reverse index over `TOOL_GROUPS`, is what that reconstruction looks the `ToolItem` back up by). `fight_end` (built ad hoc in `confirmFightEnd`, not a `ToolItem`) is the one action that still sends and stores a real `description`.

`Annotate.tsx` builds one `describe(e)` closure (over `redName`/`blueName` and the fight's own `corner_swap` spans, via `utils/describeEvent.ts` + `isFrameSwapped`) and passes it down through `AnnotationPanel` to both `AnnotationList` and `AnnotationTimeline`, which call it instead of reading `e.description` anywhere (list rows, timeline clip titles, the hover tooltip) — so marking or editing a `corner_swap` span updates already-logged strikes' displayed fighter name immediately, with no backfill.

**Span annotation (`O`/`P` keys → `createEvent({ kind: 'round'|'corner_swap'|'excluded', ... })`).** `round`/`corner_swap`/`excluded` rows are the range-shaped `kind`s of the same `fight_events` table (`frame` = start, `end_frame` nullable). `round` events are auto-seeded server-side from the AI-segmented `rounds` table the first time Annotate fetches `source='label'` events for a fight, and rendered as draggable blocks in `AnnotationTimeline`'s ROUNDS lane (edge-drag calls `onUpdateSpan`, which `PUT`s `frame`/`end_frame`). `corner_swap`/`excluded` are start/end toggles: `Annotate.tsx`'s `openSpanRef` tracks the in-flight event id per kind so the second `O`/`P` press knows what to close — `toggleSpan()` creates one with `end_frame=null` on open, `PUT`s `end_frame` to close it. `AnnotationTimeline` renders an open span dashed, running to the current playhead. `Annotate.tsx` derives its `events` (kind='point') and `spans` (kind!='point') arrays from the one `useEvents(fightId, { source: 'label' })` result via `useMemo`.

**"Finish Labeling" is gated.** `POST /fights/{id}/finish-labeling` (via `handleFinishLabeling`) 409s until every detected round has a confirmed `round`-kind label event — the backend check (`rounds_fully_annotated`), not anything client-side.

**Fight-state marks are change points, not spans.** `W`/`F`/`G` (STRIKING/CLINCH/GROUND) log a single-frame `label_event`; `AnnotationTimeline`'s STATE lane derives contiguous segments by pairing each mark with the next one chronologically (last mark implicitly runs to the end of the timeline in the UI — the harness-side derivation in `ai/eval/labels_db.py` instead runs it to the end of its round, which matters when exporting).

</system-reminder>

## 6. Chart library

**None.** No `recharts`, `chart.js`, `d3`, `visx`, `victory`, `nivo`, `apexcharts`, `plotly`, or `echarts` in `package.json` or `package-lock.json`, and nothing chart-related in `node_modules`. Total runtime deps are just `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router-dom`, `axios` (unused).

Every visualisation is **hand-written inline SVG**. `PaceChart.tsx` is the reference implementation — fixed `viewBox="0 0 900 H"`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, manual `x()`/`y()` scale functions, path strings built with `.map().join(' ')`, gradient `<defs>`:

```tsx
const W = 900, H = height, padB = 22, padT = 12;
const maxY = Math.max(4, ...redPace, ...bluePace);
const x = (i: number) => (i / (n - 1)) * W;
const y = (v: number) => H - padB - (v / maxY) * (H - padB - padT);
const line = (arr: number[]) =>
  arr.map((v, i) => `${i === 0 ? 'M' : 'L'}${x(i).toFixed(1)},${y(v).toFixed(1)}`).join(' ');
const area = (arr: number[]) => `${line(arr)} L${W},${H - padB} L0,${H - padB} Z`;
```

## 2. `ai/` — pipeline and the existing eval harness

### Pipeline stages
`/Users/filip.culig/Developer/fight-ai/ai/pipeline.py` orchestrates (`main.py` is argparse only). Fully in-memory — no intermediate files; Postgres is the only store.

`detect_fighters()` → `track_fighters()` → `assign_corners()` → `extract_scoreboard_samples()` → `segment_fights()` → `process_fight()` (writes DB).

States in `/Users/filip.culig/Developer/fight-ai/ai/models/FightProcessingState.py`: `validating, invalid, queued, detecting, tracking, pose, corners, scoreboard, segmenting, analyzing, completed, labeling_in_progress, labeling_complete, failed`.

### The eval harness — `/Users/filip.culig/Developer/fight-ai/ai/eval/` (it already exists and is substantial)

| File | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `score.py` | The scoring engine — strike P/R/F1, state accuracy, round IoU |
| `sanity.py` | 9 label-free plausibility checks |
| `corner_accuracy.py` | Label-free corner correctness vs. kit colour |
| `corner_swap_check.py` | `inject_swap()` + `measure_recall()` — labeller swap recall |
| `videocheck.py` | Full-decode integrity: `reported_frames`, `decoded_frames`, `missing_ratio`, `truncated` |
| `predictions.py` | Reads `fight_events WHERE source='prediction'` + `rounds` out of Postgres |
| `labels_db.py` | Builds `FightLabels` from `fight_events WHERE source='label'` |
| `schema.py` | Ground-truth JSON format + taxonomy + `PIPELINE_ACTION_MAP` |
| `report_io.py` | JSON persistence + provenance envelope |
| `cli.py` | `export, video, sanity, score, agreement, inject-swap, corner-swap-recall, summary` |

### Concrete metric names already computed

**`score.py` — `Report(video, fps, scored_minutes, strikes, state, rounds)`**

`StrikeScore`: `detection` (a `PRF` with `.tp/.fp/.fn/.precision/.recall/.f1`), `tolerance_frames`, `fighter_correct/_total` → `fighter_accuracy` (documented as **circular** — "corner read-back", not attribution), `family_correct/_total` → `family_accuracy`, `target_correct/_total` → `target_accuracy`, `landed_correct/_total` → `landed_accuracy`, `nonspecific_matches`, `family_confusion` (dict keyed `(truth, pred)`), `matched_offsets` → `offset_bias` (median signed) and `offset_jitter` (median absolute), `missed` (FN list), `spurious` (FP list).

`StateScore`: `frames_scored`, `frames_correct` → `accuracy`, `confusion` (3×3 over `STATES = ("STRIKING","CLINCH","GROUND")`), `gt_transitions_per_min`, `pred_transitions_per_min`, `gt_median_dwell_secs`, `pred_median_dwell_secs`.

`RoundScore`: `matched` (list of `(round, iou, start_delta_secs, end_delta_secs)`) → `mean_iou`, `gt_count`, `pred_count` → `count_correct`.

Matching: optimal Hungarian (`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment`) on temporal offset, `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_SECS = 0.25`, fighter ignored unless `--strict-fighter`.

**`sanity.py` — 9 named checks** (each a `Check(name, value, passed, detail, band)`):
`"events inside rounds"`, `"no simultaneous mutual strikes"`, `"no duplicate events"`, `"state does not flap"`, `"state dwell is physical"`, `"strike rate is plausible"`, `"no short interior rounds"`, `"round breaks are real breaks"`, `"round count fits video length"`. Bands: `MAX_OUT_OF_ROUND_RATIO=0.0`, `MAX_MUTUAL_STRIKE_EVENT_RATIO=0.02`, `MAX_STATE_TRANSITIONS_PER_MIN=15.0`, `MIN_STATE_MEDIAN_DWELL_SECS=1.0`, `MIN_STRIKES_PER_MIN=5.0`, `MAX_STRIKES_PER_MIN=60.0`. Plus `type_counts` and `out_of_round_types` Counters.

**`corner_accuracy.py` — `CornerAccuracy(fight_id, decisive_frames, correct, runs)`** → `.accuracy`. Thresholds: `<0.5` = `[FAIL]` inverted, `<0.9` = `[WARN]` intermittent, no decisive frames = *unverified, not a pass*.

**`corner_swap_check.py` — `RecallResult(detected, matched_span, start_error_frames, end_error_frames, corner_swap_spans)`**.

### Concrete metric names already computed

**`score.py` — `Report(video, fps, scored_minutes, strikes, state, rounds)`**

`StrikeScore`: `detection` (a `PRF` with `.tp/.fp/.fn/.precision/.recall/.f1`), `tolerance_frames`, `fighter_correct/_total` → `fighter_accuracy` (documented as **circular** — "corner read-back", not attribution), `family_correct/_total` → `family_accuracy`, `target_correct/_total` → `target_accuracy`, `landed_correct/_total` → `landed_accuracy`, `nonspecific_matches`, `family_confusion` (dict keyed `(truth, pred)`), `matched_offsets` → `offset_bias` (median signed) and `offset_jitter` (median absolute), `missed` (FN list), `spurious` (FP list).

Matching: optimal Hungarian (`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment`) on temporal offset, `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_SECS = 0.25`, fighter ignored unless `--strict-fighter`.

**`sanity.py` — 9 named checks** (each a `Check(name, value, passed, detail, band)`):
`"events inside rounds"`, `"no simultaneous mutual strikes"`, `"no duplicate events"`, `"state does not flap"`, `"state dwell is physical"`, `"strike rate is plausible"`, `"no short interior rounds"`, `"round breaks are real breaks"`, `"round count fits video length"`. Bands: `MAX_OUT_OF_ROUND_RATIO=0.0`, `MAX_MUTUAL_STRIKE_EVENT_RATIO=0.02`, `MAX_STATE_TRANSITIONS_PER_MIN=15.0`, `MIN_STATE_MEDIAN_DWELL_SECS=1.0`, `MIN_STRIKES_PER_MIN=5.0`, `MAX_STRIKES_PER_MIN=60.0`. Plus `type_counts` and `out_of_round_types` Counters.

**`corner_accuracy.py` — `CornerAccuracy(fight_id, decisive_frames, correct, runs)`** → `.accuracy`. Thresholds: `<0.5` = `[FAIL]` inverted, `<0.9` = `[WARN]` intermittent, no decisive frames = *unverified, not a pass*.

Semantics you need:
- `source` — `'prediction'` (pipeline, raw SQL in `fight_processing.py`) vs `'label'` (Annotate UI, via `event_service.py`). **Every query needs an explicit `source` filter or it blends the two.**
- `kind` — `'point'` | `'round'` | `'corner_swap'` | `'excluded'`. Range kinds use `frame` as start + `end_frame`; `end_frame IS NULL` on a range kind = span still open (a real warning state).
- `corner` (0/1) is label-only, a *track slot*, not a person. `fighter_id` (FK) is prediction-only, a resolved identity. Enforced by CHECK.
- `value` on range kinds = round number (as text) or exclusion reason.

## 2. `ai/` — pipeline and the existing eval harness

### Pipeline stages

| File | What it computes |
|---|---|

### Concrete metric names already computed

**`score.py` — `Report(video, fps, scored_minutes, strikes, state, rounds)`**

`StrikeScore`: `detection` (a `PRF` with `.tp/.fp/.fn/.precision/.recall/.f1`), `tolerance_frames`, `fighter_correct/_total` → `fighter_accuracy` (documented as **circular** — "corner read-back", not attribution), `family_correct/_total` → `family_accuracy`, `target_correct/_total` → `target_accuracy`, `landed_correct/_total` → `landed_accuracy`, `nonspecific_matches`, `family_confusion` (dict keyed `(truth, pred)`), `matched_offsets` → `offset_bias` (median signed) and `offset_jitter` (median absolute), `missed` (FN list), `spurious` (FP list).

`StateScore`: `frames_scored`, `frames_correct` → `accuracy`, `confusion` (3×3 over `STATES = ("STRIKING","CLINCH","GROUND")`), `gt_transitions_per_min`, `pred_transitions_per_min`, `gt_median_dwell_secs`, `pred_median_dwell_secs`.

`RoundScore`: `matched` (list of `(round, iou, start_delta_secs, end_delta_secs)`) → `mean_iou`, `gt_count`, `pred_count` → `count_correct`.

Matching: optimal Hungarian (`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment`) on temporal offset, `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_SECS = 0.25`, fighter ignored unless `--strict-fighter`.

**`sanity.py` — 9 named checks** (each a `Check(name, value, passed, detail, band)`):
`"events inside rounds"`, `"no simultaneous mutual strikes"`, `"no duplicate events"`, `"state does not flap"`, `"state dwell is physical"`, `"strike rate is plausible"`, `"no short interior rounds"`, `"round breaks are real breaks"`, `"round count fits video length"`. Bands: `MAX_OUT_OF_ROUND_RATIO=0.0`, `MAX_MUTUAL_STRIKE_EVENT_RATIO=0.02`, `MAX_STATE_TRANSITIONS_PER_MIN=15.0`, `MIN_STATE_MEDIAN_DWELL_SECS=1.0`, `MIN_STRIKES_PER_MIN=5.0`, `MAX_STRIKES_PER_MIN=60.0`. Plus `type_counts` and `out_of_round_types` Counters.

**`corner_accuracy.py` — `CornerAccuracy(fight_id, decisive_frames, correct, runs)`** → `.accuracy`. Thresholds: `<0.5` = `[FAIL]` inverted, `<0.9` = `[WARN]` intermittent, no decisive frames = *unverified, not a pass*.

**`corner_swap_check.py` — `RecallResult(detected, matched_span, start_error_frames, end_error_frames, corner_swap_spans)`**.

## 4. Labelling tooling and ground-truth format

There is **no standalone labeller**. `ai/eval/label.py` (OpenCV tool) was deleted — only a stale `.pyc` remains at `ai/eval/__pycache__/label.cpython-314.pyc`.

Labelling is the frontend Annotate page: `/Users/filip.culig/Developer/fight-ai/frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx` + `/Users/filip.culig/Developer/fight-ai/frontend/src/components/annotate/` (`taxonomy.ts` defines `TOOL_GROUPS`/`KEYMAP`, `AnnotationTimeline.tsx`, `EventPalette.tsx`, `FightEndModal.tsx`, `KeyboardLegend.tsx`).

**Two ground-truth formats:**

1. **In DB** — `fight_events WHERE source='label'`. Point actions come from `taxonomy.ts`: `jab, cross, left_hook, right_hook, left_uppercut, right_uppercut, calf_kick, low_kick, middle_kick, high_kick, elbow, clinch_knee, ground_knee, clinch_punch, ground_punch, takedown_landed, takedown_attempt, takedown_defended, submission, knockdown, fight_end, state_striking, state_clinch, state_ground`.

2. **On disk** — `ai/eval/labels/<video_stem>.json`, committed to git, produced by `python -m eval.cli export <video>`. Defined by `FightLabels` in `schema.py`:
```json
{"video","fps","frame_count","labeler","labeled_at","notes",
 "rounds":[{round,start,end}], "excluded":[{start,end,reason}],
 "states":[{start,end,state}], "strikes":[{frame,fighter,family,target,landed}],
 "corner_swaps":[{start,end}], "takedowns":[{frame,fighter}]}
```
Taxonomy: `FAMILIES = (jab, cross, hook, uppercut, elbow, knee, kick, punch)`, `TARGETS = (head, body, leg, unknown)`, `FIGHTERS = (red, blue)`, `STATES = (STRIKING, CLINCH, GROUND)`. Frames 1-based.

The DB→disk mapping is `LABEL_FAMILY_MAP` and `STATE_ACTION_MAP` in `labels_db.py`; the pipeline→taxonomy mapping is `PIPELINE_ACTION_MAP` in `schema.py`. Second passes go to `labels/<stem>.<labeler>.json`; the agreement ceiling to `labels/<stem>.agreement.json`.

`export` refuses any fight with `labeled_at IS NULL` (raises `NotLabeled`).

    """Read every persisted event for a video and map it into the label taxonomy."""
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        fight_id, video_path, fps, _ = lookup_fight(db, video)

        for r in db.execute(

            preds.rounds.append(
                Round(start=r.start_frame, end=r.end_frame, round=r.round_number)
            )

        rows = db.execute(
            text("SELECT frame, description, action, success, state FROM fight_events "
                 "WHERE fight_id = :fid AND source = 'prediction' ORDER BY frame, id"),

        for row in rows:

            m = _STRIKE_RE.match(desc)
            if m:
                corner = "red" if m.group(1) == "fighter_red" else "blue"
                action = row.action or m.group(2)
                family, target = PIPELINE_ACTION_MAP.get(action, ("punch", "unknown"))
                preds.strikes.append(PredictedStrike(

                    fighter=corner,

                    target=target,

                continue

            if row.state:
                preds.state_changes.append(StateChange(frame=row.frame, state=row.state))
                continue

            # Fallback for rows written before the structured `state` column

            m = _STATE_RE.search(desc)
            if m:
                preds.state_changes.append(StateChange(frame=row.frame, state=m.group(1)))

        fc = db.execute(
            text("SELECT MAX(frame) AS mx FROM fighter_frames WHERE fight_id = :fid"),
            {"fid": fight_id},
        ).scalar()
        preds.frame_count = int(fc or 0)

        return preds
    finally:
        db.close()

# Training Lab (`/lab`) — findings and plan

> **Status: draft.** Awaiting answers on design-project access, scope, and the
> reference↔run pairing mechanism. Findings below are verified against the live
> database and working tree on 2026-09-14.

## Context

Fight.AI turns MMA video into structured events. The rule cascade that emits
strikes and fight state is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model,
and everything about that depends on measured accuracy — which today lives only
in CLI stdout (`python -m eval.cli summary | score | sanity`).

`frontend/TRAINING_LAB_BRIEF.md` (717 lines, written 10 Sep) specs a `/lab` page
for this. **No `/lab` code exists** — `grep -rniE "\blab\b|training.?lab"
frontend/src` returns nothing.

Since the brief was written, two commits changed the model it assumes:

- `fc13725` added `fights.purpose` (`training_data` | `reference` | `ai_labeled`),
  set once at upload and never changed. A fight's pipeline never re-runs.
- `9bd41d1` merged `label_events` + `label_spans` into one `fight_events` table
  with `source` / `kind` discriminators. **The brief's Appendix cites the dropped
  tables and is stale.**

The user's workflow is now: upload the bout once as `reference` and hand-label
it; then upload the *same source video* again, once per pipeline version, as
`ai_labeled`. Accuracy is a **cross-fight** comparison between two fight ids.

## Verified state of the data (2026-09-14)

```
 id |               video_path               | fps |       state       |   purpose
 60 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4    |  50 | labeling_complete | reference
 62 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4  |  50 | completed         | ai_labeled
```

Both files are 612,577,927 bytes — the same video uploaded twice. Both rows
report 43,100 frames, 50 fps, and the same fighter ids (red 15, blue 16).

| | fight 60 (reference) | fight 62 (pipeline run 1) |
|---|---|---|
| strike rows | **227 labels** (114 red / 113 blue) | **147 predictions** (78 / 69) |
| state marks | 5 (`striking` 3, `clinch` 2, **ground 0**) | **0** |
| rounds | 1025–10025 · 13900–22900 · 26525–35525 | **byte-identical** |
| `fighter_frames` | 74,083 rows, all with keypoints | **74,083**, all with keypoints |
| `corner_swap` spans | **14**, covering 11,429 of 27,000 round frames = **42.3%** | — |
| `excluded` spans | 1 (35508–35525) | — |
| round label spans | seeded from `rounds`, one shared microsecond `created_at`, **never adjusted** | auto-seeded (Annotate was opened on it) |

Ground-truth class distribution on fight 60 (top): `left_hook·head` 77,
`jab·head` 35, `cross·head` 30, `right_hook·head` 22, `low_kick` 14,
`high_kick` 14, `calf_kick` 10, `middle_kick` 9, `cross·body` 4,
`right_uppercut` 4, `clinch_knee` 3, `left_uppercut` 3, `right_hook·body` 1,
`jab·body` 1. No ground-and-pound, no elbows, no takedowns — a standing fight.

Pipeline vocabulary on fight 62: `jab_head` 25, `hook_body` 24, `low_kick` 21,
`jab_body` 20, `hook_head` 16, `cross_head` 15, `middle_kick` 14, `cross_body` 9,
`head_kick` 1, `uppercut_head` 1, `uppercut_body` 1. **No knee, no elbow, no
ground/clinch punch.**

## Blockers — no honest number can be shown until these are fixed

1. **The scorer cannot see any prediction.** `ai/eval/predictions.py:130`
   gates the strike branch on `_STRIKE_RE.match(row.description)`, but migration
   `f0a1b2c3d4e5` NULLed `description` on every non-`fight_end` point row.
   Verified: all 147 prediction rows on fight 62 have `description IS NULL` and
   `fighter_id` populated. Today `score` would report P/R/F1 = 0 — not because
   the pipeline is bad, but because nothing is loaded.
   Fix: read `action` + derive corner from `fighter_id == fights.red_fighter_id`
   (the same rule `frontend/src/utils/liveStats.ts:attributedCorner` already uses).
2. **`score.py` is single-fight.** It loads labels and predictions for one
   `video`. The new model needs labels from fight A and predictions from fight B.
3. **Nothing records which pipeline version produced a run**, and nothing links
   fight 62 back to fight 60. Today it is inferable only from the `_2` filename
   suffix and `created_at`. `ai/manifest.py` exists but is never called.
4. **No eval persistence and no HTTP surface.** `backend/app/api/routes/` has
   zero metrics endpoints; `--json` exists only on `sanity` and `score`;
   `corner_accuracy` and `corner-swap-recall` print only.
5. **Fight state is unmeasurable.** `SELECT state, count(*) FROM fight_events
   WHERE state IS NOT NULL` returns **zero rows across the entire database**.
   The pipeline has never persisted a state change.

## Changes to what the page should display

Grounded in the numbers above; each replaces or re-scopes a part of the brief.

1. **Make the run axis the spine of section E, not a footnote.** The brief's E8
   trend chart is the last item; under the new workflow it is the primary object.
   E should open with "Runs against BILANDZIC vs LUPASCU" — one row per
   `ai_labeled` fight, newest first, each with P/R/F1 and the delta vs the
   previous run. The trend line is that table plotted.
2. **Add a reference-pair provenance card**, asserting the two fights really are
   the same bout: same byte size, same `reported_frames`, same fps, same fighter
   ids. A mismatch is critical — every frame-indexed label would be misaligned.
3. **Add run-to-run determinism, independent of ground truth.** Because each run
   is a fresh pass over the identical video, a diff against the previous run is
   free and answers "did my change do anything at all?" before F1 is consulted:
   rounds identical (60/62 are), `fighter_frames` row count identical (74,083
   both), strike count 147 → next. The brief has nothing like this.
4. **Lead E3 with truth-vs-predicted counts per class, not accuracy tiles.** The
   real story here is invisible in a "target zone 71.8%" tile: the pipeline
   predicted `hook_body` 24× and `jab_body` 20× against 1 and 1 in ground truth.
   It is systematically calling body. Show the paired counts first.
5. **Compute "structurally impossible" from the run's own vocabulary.** The brief
   hardcodes elbow as `Always a miss`. Fight 62 emits no knee either, so the 3
   labelled `clinch_knee` are guaranteed FN. Derive this per run.
6. **Fight state renders `Not measured` with its reason** — "the pipeline
   persisted 0 state changes" — not an empty dumbbell chart.
7. **Corner swaps are the headline of section C, not a footnote.** 42.3% of
   labelled round time on fight 60 sits inside a marked swap, against the brief's
   illustrative `≥ 4.4%`. Per `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` this does
   *not* corrupt the label→keypoint join, but it does make "corner read-back"
   worthless on this pair and per-fighter stats unreliable for 42% of the fight.
8. **Replace round IoU with `Seeded — not verified` plus cross-run agreement.**
   Fight 60's round spans are byte-identical to its own `rounds` row with a
   shared microsecond timestamp, and 62's rounds equal 60's exactly — IoU is
   100% and circular twice over. The honest signal is determinism, not accuracy.
9. **Split the training-progress hero in two.** 227 of the 300 strikes are on a
   `reference` fight, which is explicitly held out of training. One meter for
   training ground truth (`purpose='training_data'` only), one for evaluation
   ground truth (`reference`).
10. **Retire the `⚠ Both` role warning.** `purpose` makes training/eval overlap
    structurally impossible. The live risk in the new model is a video stem
    uploaded under two purposes, or a run paired to the wrong reference.

## Open questions

- Access to the Claude Design project (`f026815c…`, `Training Lab.html` + 6
  asset files) — DesignSync needs a one-time `/design-login`.
- Scope of the first implementation pass.
- How a run is tied to its reference fight.

Schema: 5 tables — `fighters`, `fights`, `rounds`, `fighter_frames`, `fight_events`.

`fights.purpose` is 'training_data' | 'reference' | 'ai_labeled', set once at upload.

- fight 60 = `fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4`, purpose='reference', 227 label strikes, 14 corner_swap spans, 5 state marks, rounds 1025-10025 / 13900-22900 / 26525-35525
- fight 62 = `fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4`, purpose='ai_labeled', 147 prediction strikes, same rounds byte-identical, same fighter ids (red 15, blue 16), identical file size

2. `score.py` is single-video: it loads labels and predictions for one video. It needs a cross-fight mode.

6. **Ordering**: what must land first so a real (non-zero) F1 for fight 60 vs 62 appears with the least work.

Be concrete: real file paths, real function names, real column names. Flag anything in my context above that you find to be wrong when you read the code.

"""Rough preview of the 60-vs-62 score: optimal 1:1 temporal matching within a
tolerance, restricted to round spans, mirroring ai/eval/score.py's contract.
Read-only; throwaway."""
import csv, sys
from itertools import product

ROUNDS = [(1025, 10025), (13900, 22900), (26525, 35525)]
EXCLUDED = [(35508, 35525)]
FPS = 50

LABEL_FAMILY = {
    "jab": "jab", "cross": "cross",
    "left_hook": "hook", "right_hook": "hook",
    "left_uppercut": "uppercut", "right_uppercut": "uppercut",
    "elbow": "elbow",
    "calf_kick": ("kick", "leg"), "low_kick": ("kick", "leg"),
    "middle_kick": ("kick", "body"), "high_kick": ("kick", "head"),
    "clinch_knee": ("knee", "unknown"), "ground_knee": ("knee", "unknown"),
    "clinch_punch": ("punch", "unknown"), "ground_punch": ("punch", "unknown"),
}
PRED_MAP = {
    "jab_head": ("jab", "head"), "jab_body": ("jab", "body"),
    "cross_head": ("cross", "head"), "cross_body": ("cross", "body"),
    "hook_head": ("hook", "head"), "hook_body": ("hook", "body"),
    "uppercut_head": ("uppercut", "head"), "uppercut_body": ("uppercut", "body"),
    "low_kick": ("kick", "leg"), "middle_kick": ("kick", "body"),
    "head_kick": ("kick", "head"),
    "clinch_knee": ("knee", "unknown"), "ground_knee": ("knee", "unknown"),
    "clinch_punch": ("punch", "unknown"), "ground_punch": ("punch", "unknown"),
}


def in_scope(f):
    if any(a <= f <= b for a, b in EXCLUDED):
        return False
    return any(a <= f <= b for a, b in ROUNDS)


def load_labels(path):
    out = []
    for frame, action, target, corner in csv.reader(open(path)):
        frame = int(frame)
        if not in_scope(frame):
            continue
        m = LABEL_FAMILY.get(action)
        if m is None:
            continue
        fam, tgt = (m, target or "unknown") if isinstance(m, str) else m
        out.append({"frame": frame, "family": fam, "target": tgt,
                    "corner": int(corner), "action": action})
    return out


def load_preds(path):
    out = []
    for frame, action, corner in csv.reader(open(path)):
        frame = int(frame)
        if not in_scope(frame):
            continue
        fam, tgt = PRED_MAP.get(action, ("punch", "unknown"))
        out.append({"frame": frame, "family": fam, "target": tgt,
                    "corner": int(corner), "action": action})
    return out


def match(gt, pr, tol):
    """Optimal 1:1 on |offset| via scipy if available, else greedy by distance."""
    pairs = [(i, j, abs(g["frame"] - p["frame"]))
             for (i, g), (j, p) in product(enumerate(gt), enumerate(pr))
             if abs(g["frame"] - p["frame"]) <= tol]
    pairs.sort(key=lambda t: t[2])
    used_g, used_p, matched = set(), set(), []
    for i, j, d in pairs:
        if i in used_g or j in used_p:
            continue
        used_g.add(i); used_p.add(j); matched.append((i, j))
    return matched


def report(gt, pr, tol):
    matched = match(gt, pr, tol)
    tp, fp, fn = len(matched), len(pr) - len(matched), len(gt) - len(matched)
    prec = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
    rec = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
    f1 = 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec) if prec + rec else 0.0
    offsets = sorted(pr[j]["frame"] - gt[i]["frame"] for i, j in matched)
    bias = offsets[len(offsets) // 2] if offsets else 0
    jitter = sorted(abs(o - bias) for o in offsets)
    jitter = jitter[len(jitter) // 2] if jitter else 0

    spec = [(i, j) for i, j in matched if gt[i]["target"] != "unknown"
            and pr[j]["target"] != "unknown"]
    fam_ok = sum(1 for i, j in spec if gt[i]["family"] == pr[j]["family"])
    tgt_ok = sum(1 for i, j in spec if gt[i]["target"] == pr[j]["target"])
    corner_ok = sum(1 for i, j in matched if gt[i]["corner"] == pr[j]["corner"])

    print(f"\n--- tolerance +/-{tol} f ({tol/FPS:.2f} s) ---")
    print(f"labelled {len(gt)} | predicted {len(pr)}")
    print(f"TP {tp}  FP {fp}  FN {fn}")
    print(f"P {prec*100:.1f}%  R {rec*100:.1f}%  F1 {f1*100:.1f}%")
    print(f"bias {bias:+d} f ({bias/FPS*1000:+.0f} ms)  jitter {jitter} f")
    if spec:
        print(f"family {fam_ok}/{len(spec)} = {fam_ok/len(spec)*100:.1f}%  "
              f"target {tgt_ok}/{len(spec)} = {tgt_ok/len(spec)*100:.1f}%")
    print(f"corner read-back {corner_ok}/{tp} = "
          f"{corner_ok/tp*100:.1f}% (circular)" if tp else "")
    return matched


gt = load_labels(sys.argv[1])
pr = load_preds(sys.argv[2])
print(f"in-scope: {len(gt)} labels, {len(pr)} predictions")

for tol in (12, 25, 50):
    m = report(gt, pr, tol)

# class-level truth vs predicted counts at the family/target level
from collections import Counter
gc = Counter((g["family"], g["target"]) for g in gt)
pc = Counter((p["family"], p["target"]) for p in pr)
print("\n--- class counts (truth vs predicted) ---")
for k in sorted(set(gc) | set(pc)):
    print(f"{k[0]:9s} {k[1]:8s}  truth {gc.get(k,0):4d}   pred {pc.get(k,0):4d}")

# Training Lab (`/lab`) — findings and plan

> **Status: draft.** Awaiting answers on design-project access, scope, and the
> reference↔run pairing mechanism. Findings below are verified against the live
> database and working tree on 2026-09-14.

## Context

Fight.AI turns MMA video into structured events. The rule cascade that emits
strikes and fight state is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model,
and everything about that depends on measured accuracy — which today lives only
in CLI stdout (`python -m eval.cli summary | score | sanity`).

`frontend/TRAINING_LAB_BRIEF.md` (717 lines, written 10 Sep) specs a `/lab` page
for this. **No `/lab` code exists** — `grep -rniE "\blab\b|training.?lab"
frontend/src` returns nothing.

Since the brief was written, two commits changed the model it assumes:

- `fc13725` added `fights.purpose` (`training_data` | `reference` | `ai_labeled`),
  set once at upload and never changed. A fight's pipeline never re-runs.
- `9bd41d1` merged `label_events` + `label_spans` into one `fight_events` table
  with `source` / `kind` discriminators. **The brief's Appendix cites the dropped
  tables and is stale.**

The user's workflow is now: upload the bout once as `reference` and hand-label
it; then upload the *same source video* again, once per pipeline version, as
`ai_labeled`. Accuracy is a **cross-fight** comparison between two fight ids.

## Verified state of the data (2026-09-14)

```
 id |               video_path               | fps |       state       |   purpose
 60 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4    |  50 | labeling_complete | reference
 62 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4  |  50 | completed         | ai_labeled
```

Both files are 612,577,927 bytes — the same video uploaded twice. Both rows
report 43,100 frames, 50 fps, and the same fighter ids (red 15, blue 16).

| | fight 60 (reference) | fight 62 (pipeline run 1) |
|---|---|---|
| strike rows | **227 labels** (114 red / 113 blue) | **147 predictions** (78 / 69) |
| state marks | 5 (`striking` 3, `clinch` 2, **ground 0**) | **0** |
| rounds | 1025–10025 · 13900–22900 · 26525–35525 | **byte-identical** |
| `fighter_frames` | 74,083 rows, all with keypoints | **74,083**, all with keypoints |
| `corner_swap` spans | **14**, covering 11,429 of 27,000 round frames = **42.3%** | — |
| `excluded` spans | 1 (35508–35525) | — |
| round label spans | seeded from `rounds`, one shared microsecond `created_at`, **never adjusted** | auto-seeded (Annotate was opened on it) |

Ground-truth class distribution on fight 60 (top): `left_hook·head` 77,
`jab·head` 35, `cross·head` 30, `right_hook·head` 22, `low_kick` 14,
`high_kick` 14, `calf_kick` 10, `middle_kick` 9, `cross·body` 4,
`right_uppercut` 4, `clinch_knee` 3, `left_uppercut` 3, `right_hook·body` 1,
`jab·body` 1. No ground-and-pound, no elbows, no takedowns — a standing fight.

Pipeline vocabulary on fight 62: `jab_head` 25, `hook_body` 24, `low_kick` 21,
`jab_body` 20, `hook_head` 16, `cross_head` 15, `middle_kick` 14, `cross_body` 9,
`head_kick` 1, `uppercut_head` 1, `uppercut_body` 1. **No knee, no elbow, no
ground/clinch punch.**

## Blockers — no honest number can be shown until these are fixed

1. **The scorer cannot see any prediction.** `ai/eval/predictions.py:130`
   gates the strike branch on `_STRIKE_RE.match(row.description)`, but migration
   `f0a1b2c3d4e5` NULLed `description` on every non-`fight_end` point row.
   Verified: all 147 prediction rows on fight 62 have `description IS NULL` and
   `fighter_id` populated. Today `score` would report P/R/F1 = 0 — not because
   the pipeline is bad, but because nothing is loaded.
   Fix: read `action` + derive corner from `fighter_id == fights.red_fighter_id`
   (the same rule `frontend/src/utils/liveStats.ts:attributedCorner` already uses).
2. **`score.py` is single-fight.** It loads labels and predictions for one
   `video`. The new model needs labels from fight A and predictions from fight B.
3. **Nothing records which pipeline version produced a run**, and nothing links
   fight 62 back to fight 60. Today it is inferable only from the `_2` filename
   suffix and `created_at`. `ai/manifest.py` exists but is never called.
4. **No eval persistence and no HTTP surface.** `backend/app/api/routes/` has
   zero metrics endpoints; `--json` exists only on `sanity` and `score`;
   `corner_accuracy` and `corner-swap-recall` print only.
5. **Fight state is unmeasurable.** `SELECT state, count(*) FROM fight_events
   WHERE state IS NOT NULL` returns **zero rows across the entire database**.
   The pipeline has never persisted a state change.

## Changes to what the page should display

Grounded in the numbers above; each replaces or re-scopes a part of the brief.

1. **Make the run axis the spine of section E, not a footnote.** The brief's E8
   trend chart is the last item; under the new workflow it is the primary object.
   E should open with "Runs against BILANDZIC vs LUPASCU" — one row per
   `ai_labeled` fight, newest first, each with P/R/F1 and the delta vs the
   previous run. The trend line is that table plotted.
2. **Add a reference-pair provenance card**, asserting the two fights really are
   the same bout: same byte size, same `reported_frames`, same fps, same fighter
   ids. A mismatch is critical — every frame-indexed label would be misaligned.
3. **Add run-to-run determinism, independent of ground truth.** Because each run
   is a fresh pass over the identical video, a diff against the previous run is
   free and answers "did my change do anything at all?" before F1 is consulted:
   rounds identical (60/62 are), `fighter_frames` row count identical (74,083
   both), strike count 147 → next. The brief has nothing like this.
4. **Lead E3 with truth-vs-predicted counts per class, not accuracy tiles.** The
   real story here is invisible in a "target zone 71.8%" tile: the pipeline
   predicted `hook_body` 24× and `jab_body` 20× against 1 and 1 in ground truth.
   It is systematically calling body. Show the paired counts first.
5. **Compute "structurally impossible" from the run's own vocabulary.** The brief
   hardcodes elbow as `Always a miss`. Fight 62 emits no knee either, so the 3
   labelled `clinch_knee` are guaranteed FN. Derive this per run.
6. **Fight state renders `Not measured` with its reason** — "the pipeline
   persisted 0 state changes" — not an empty dumbbell chart.
7. **Corner swaps are the headline of section C, not a footnote.** 42.3% of
   labelled round time on fight 60 sits inside a marked swap, against the brief's
   illustrative `≥ 4.4%`. Per `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` this does
   *not* corrupt the label→keypoint join, but it does make "corner read-back"
   worthless on this pair and per-fighter stats unreliable for 42% of the fight.
8. **Replace round IoU with `Seeded — not verified` plus cross-run agreement.**
   Fight 60's round spans are byte-identical to its own `rounds` row with a
   shared microsecond timestamp, and 62's rounds equal 60's exactly — IoU is
   100% and circular twice over. The honest signal is determinism, not accuracy.
9. **Split the training-progress hero in two.** 227 of the 300 strikes are on a
   `reference` fight, which is explicitly held out of training. One meter for
   training ground truth (`purpose='training_data'` only), one for evaluation
   ground truth (`reference`).
10. **Retire the `⚠ Both` role warning.** `purpose` makes training/eval overlap
    structurally impossible. The live risk in the new model is a video stem
    uploaded under two purposes, or a run paired to the wrong reference.

## Open questions

- Access to the Claude Design project (`f026815c…`, `Training Lab.html` + 6
  asset files) — DesignSync needs a one-time `/design-login`.
- Scope of the first implementation pass.
- How a run is tied to its reference fight.

## Preview of the number the page will show

I reimplemented the scorer's contract approximately (1:1 temporal matching,
in-round only, minus the excluded span) over the real rows, to know what the page
has to render. **Approximate** — greedy-nearest instead of the Hungarian
assignment `score.py` uses, and my own label→family map — so the real scorer will
shift these a little.

```
±12 f (0.24 s)   TP 84  FP 63  FN 143   P 57.1%  R 37.0%  F1 44.9%
±25 f (0.50 s)   TP 98  FP 49  FN 129   P 66.7%  R 43.2%  F1 52.4%
±50 f (1.00 s)   identical to ±25 — nothing further is within reach
bias −1 f (−20 ms) · jitter 2 f
family 54.2% (n=83) · target 61.4% (n=83) · corner read-back 75.0% (n=84)
```

Two things fall out of this immediately:

- **Timing is not the problem.** Bias −1 frame, jitter 2 frames, and F1 plateaus
  by ±25 f. The tolerance debate in `plan/02d-label-quality.md` is moot for this
  pair; the pipeline simply misses 129 of 227 strikes.
- **The class-count table is the finding, and no accuracy tile would show it:**

| family · target | truth | predicted |
|---|---|---|
| hook · head | **99** | **16** |
| hook · body | **1** | **24** |
| jab · head | 35 | 25 |
| jab · body | **1** | **20** |
| cross · head | 30 | 15 |
| cross · body | 4 | 9 |
| kick · leg | 24 | 21 |
| kick · body | 9 | 14 |
| kick · head | **14** | **1** |
| uppercut · head | 7 | 1 |
| knee | 3 | **0** |

  The target classifier is biased hard toward `body`, and head hooks — the single
  most common strike in the fight, 99 of 227 — are detected 16 times. That is the
  actionable number, and the brief's E3 ("Target zone 71.8%") would bury it.

**Corner read-back is 75%, not ~100% — the brief's `Circular` badge is wrong
under the new model.** The brief assumes the labeller clicked the same pipeline's
overlay, so read-back cancels out. Here the labels were read off fight 60's
overlay and scored against fight 62's independent corner assignment, so the two
can genuinely disagree. It is still not "attribution accuracy" — it is
cross-run corner agreement — but it is now a real measurement, not a tautology.

## Blockers — no honest number can be shown until these are fixed

   `ai/eval/labels/MILIDRAGOVICvsMOOSMAN.json` has ever been exported, so it
   reports "12 strikes … 288 more to reach the 300-strike target" against a
   database holding 800. Label aggregates on the page must come from
   `fight_events`, not from `ai/eval/labels/`.

I ran `eval.cli sanity` on fight 62 to see what section F renders today:

```
[PASS] events inside rounds            0/0 strikes fall outside every round
[PASS] no simultaneous mutual strikes  0 frames … (0/0 events)
[PASS] no duplicate events             0 exact duplicate rows

Six checks pass **on an empty set** because of blocker 1 — the fight has 147
predictions and the loader sees none. The two state checks don't appear at all.
This adds an honesty rule the brief doesn't have: **a check that passed with
n = 0 must render `Not evaluated`, not `Pass`.** Every check needs to carry the
population it ran over, the same way §3.1 requires of every metric.

import csv

EXCL=[(35508,35525)]

def scope(f): return any(a<=f<=b for a,b in ROUNDS) and not any(a<=f<=b for a,b in EXCL)

gt=[]

    if not scope(f): continue
    c=int(corner)
    gt.append({'frame':f,'slot':c,'person':(1-c) if swapped(f) else c})
pr=[]
for frame,action,corner in csv.reader(open('preds62.csv')):

input.new_string:
### The cross-fight model turns corner read-back into a real metric — and it fails

The brief hides corner read-back behind a `Circular` badge because the labeller
clicks the same pipeline's overlay, so a tracker swap is copied into the label
and cancels out. **That reasoning does not hold across two fights.** The labels
were read off fight 60's overlay; the predictions carry fight 62's independent
`fighter_id`. Nothing cancels.

89 of the 227 labels (39%) fall inside one of fight 60's 14 `corner_swap` spans,
so per `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` the stored `corner` is a track
slot and must be resolved to a person — at read time, by flipping inside a swap
span — before it can be compared with fight 62's `fighter_id`:

```
raw slot vs person     63/84 = 75.0%
swap-resolved          45/84 = 53.6%     ← chance, on a two-way choice
```

Fight 62 has no swap spans marked, so its `fighter_id` carries whatever swaps its
own tracker made. **That makes 53.6% genuine fighter-attribution accuracy for the
run, and it is at chance.** It is the first time this project has been able to
measure that number at all, and it deserves a tile in section E rather than a
collapsed row with a `Circular` badge.

Caveat: my matching is approximate, so some of the 84 pairs may be spurious;
treat 53.6% as "at or near chance", not as a precise figure, until the real
scorer runs.

## 5 · Frontend — the `/lab` page

Conventions to follow (all verified): React 19 + TS + Vite, `react-router-dom`,
plain `fetch` with root-relative paths, **no chart library and no CSS framework**
— every visual is hand-written inline SVG plus inline `style={{}}` referencing
`var(--token)` from `frontend/src/index.css`.

### Wiring

- `frontend/src/App.tsx` — one `<Route path="/lab" element={<Lab />} />`.
- `frontend/src/components/Header.tsx:6` — add `{ label: 'Lab', to: '/lab' }` to
  `NAV_LINKS`.
- `frontend/vite.config.ts` — add an `/eval` proxy entry. **Put the API under
  `/eval/...`, not `/lab`**, so the client route and the API path never collide
  and the `Accept: text/html` bypass the `/fights` entry needs isn't repeated.
- New files: `frontend/src/pages/Lab.tsx` + `frontend/src/components/lab/*.tsx` +
  `frontend/src/hooks/useLab*.ts`, matching the existing one-folder-per-page rule.

### Tokens to add to `index.css`

None of these exist yet. Values come from the brief §14, which were checked with
the dataviz palette validator against the card surface including CVD simulation
(see `frontend-palette-collisions`):

```css
--status-good: #0ca30c;  --status-warning: #fab219;  --status-critical: #ef4444;
--status-unverified: #94a3b8;  --status-unmeasured: #64748b;
--state-striking: #0099b0;  --state-clinch: #e64a19;  --state-ground: #9085e9;
```

Do **not** reuse `AnnotationTimeline.tsx`'s STATE colours — its CLINCH `#ff7043`
and GROUND `#ff4d4d` are ΔE 6.6 apart and GROUND is the red corner.

### Reuse, don't rebuild

| Need | Reuse |
|---|---|
| B1 palette rows | `components/annotate/taxonomy.ts` `TOOL_GROUPS` — B1 is that list joined with counts; never hardcode the actions (the palette has `submission_attempt`, the brief says `submission`) |
| R\|B split, corner attribution | `utils/liveStats.ts` `attributedCorner` |
| B3 stacked bars | `components/player/SegBar.tsx` |
| E8 trend line | model on `components/player/PaceChart.tsx` (hand-rolled SVG, fixed `viewBox`, manual scale fns) |
| Stat tiles | `components/player/MiniStat.tsx`, `.inner-tile` |
| Card header + pills + view toggle | `components/annotate/AnnotationPanel.tsx` (incl. its `localStorage` view persistence) |
| Dense clickable rows | `components/player/LiveFeed.tsx` row anatomy |
| C4 coverage strip | **extract a shared mini-strip from `components/annotate/AnnotationTimeline.tsx`** — it already draws rounds / state / swap / excluded lanes and owns `SPAN_COLOR`; this is the highest-value refactor in the whole job |
| Purpose chips | `components/FightPurposeBadge.tsx`, `types/Fight.ts` `PURPOSE_COLORS` |

New primitives that genuinely don't exist: a sortable table with a sticky header
and expandable rows (there is **no `<table>` anywhere in the codebase**), a
heatmap cell, a dumbbell row, a dot strip, a column chart, and a `StatusBadge`
rendering all five states as **icon + text** (never colour alone).

### Prerequisite on two existing pages

`?frame=N` deep links are required by C4, E9 and G2. `grep -rn "useSearchParams"
src/` returns nothing — neither `pages/Player.tsx` nor `pages/Annotate.tsx` reads
a query param today. Add `useSearchParams` to both, seeking once on mount.

## 6 · Verification

1. `docker compose up -d db`, backend on `:8000`, `npm run dev` in `frontend/`.
2. **The scorer, first and on its own** — before any UI:
   `cd ai && ../.venv/bin/python -m eval.cli score --reference 60 --run 62 --json /tmp/r.json`
   must report a non-zero F1 near the ±12 f preview above (TP 84 / FP 63 / FN 143,
   F1 ≈ 45%). If it reports 0, blocker 1 is not fixed.
3. `eval.cli sanity fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4` must stop saying
   "0 in-round strikes" and must mark n = 0 checks `Not evaluated`.
4. Insert the fight-62 run row by hand (the agreed manual step) — see §3 — then
   `curl localhost:8000/eval/runs` and confirm it lists exactly that run with
   `git_sha` `fc13725` and `constants_sha256` `b881cacf…` (verified: `constants.py`
   is unchanged between `fc13725` and the working tree, so this hash is right).
5. Open `/lab`. Check against the numbers in this plan: 800 training strikes,
   67% largest-fight share, elbow 0, 227 reference labels, 42.3% swap coverage,
   fight state `Not measured`, rounds `Seeded — not verified`.
6. Click a miss in E9 → lands on `/fights/60/annotate?frame=N` at that frame.
7. Re-run with a second `ai_labeled` upload to confirm the trend line and the
   run-to-run diff populate with two points rather than one.

## Still open

- **The Claude Design project was never readable.** After `/design-login`, import
  `Training Lab.html` and `assets/{brand.css,lab-accuracy.jsx,lab-app.jsx,
  lab-data.js,lab-parts.jsx,lab-sections.jsx}` and reconcile §5 against them —
  the design may have made layout decisions this plan should follow rather than
  re-derive.
